label: Pizza Pasta
prep: Preheat your oven to 350°F (175°C).
Grease a 9x13 inch baking dish and set aside.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil.
Add the rigatoni and cook according to the package instructions until al dente, usually about 8-10 minutes.
Drain well.
In a large skillet over medium heat, brown the ground beef until fully cooked, breaking it up into small pieces as it cooks.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Drain any excess fat.
In a large mixing bowl, combine the cooked rigatoni, browned ground beef, spaghetti sauce, Italian seasoning, and sliced mushrooms.
Stir well to ensure everything is evenly mixed.
Layer half of the pasta mixture into the prepared baking dish.
Top with half of the pepperoni slices and 1 1/2 cups of shredded mozzarella cheese.
Add the remaining pasta mixture on top of the cheese layer.
Layer the remaining pepperoni slices and sprinkle the remaining 1 1/2 cups of mozzarella cheese evenly over the top.
Cover the baking dish with aluminum foil and bake in the preheated oven for 20 minutes.
Remove the foil and continue to bake for an additional 10-15 minutes, or until the cheese is bubbly and slightly golden.
Remove from the oven and let it sit for 5 minutes before serving.
Enjoy your Pizza Pasta hot, garnished with additional Italian seasoning if desired.

label: Vegetarian Pasta Fagioli
prep: Cook pasta according to package instructions until al dente.
Drain and set aside.
In a large pot, heat a few tablespoons of olive oil over medium heat.
Add the chopped onion, celery, and carrots.
Sauté until the vegetables are softened, about 5 to 7 minutes.
Add the chopped garlic, bay leaf, and dried oregano to the pot.
Cook for another minute until the garlic is fragrant.
Stir in the roasted diced tomatoes and vegetable broth.
Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce heat and let simmer for about 15 minutes.
Rinse and drain the cannellini beans and kidney beans.
Add them to the pot.
Season the soup with salt, pepper, and crushed red pepper (if using).
Continue to simmer for another 10 minutes.
Add the cooked pasta and half of the fresh basil, chopped, to the soup.
Stir well to combine and heat through, about 2 minutes.
Taste and adjust seasoning as needed.
Remove the bay leaf before serving.
Serve the pasta fagioli hot, garnished with the remaining fresh basil, grated Parmesan cheese, and a drizzle of olive oil if desired.
Serve with slices of Italian bread on the side.

label: Lemon Glazed Madeleines
prep: Preheat your oven to 375°F (190°C).
Grease and flour a madeleine pan, using additional unsalted butter to ensure the madeleines do not stick.
Melt 4.2 ounces of unsalted butter in a small saucepan over low heat or in the microwave, then set aside to cool slightly.
In a mixing bowl, whisk together 3 eggs, ⅔ cups granulated sugar, and ¼ teaspoon salt until the mixture is light and fluffy.
Zest the lemon and add it to the egg mixture.
Save the lemon for later use in the glaze.
Sift together 6.2 ounces of all-purpose flour and 1 teaspoon of baking powder.
Gradually fold the dry ingredients into the egg mixture using a spatula.
Slowly blend in the melted butter until the batter is smooth and homogenous.
Spoon the batter into the prepared madeleine pan, filling each mold about three-quarters full.
Bake in the preheated oven for 10-12 minutes, or until the edges are golden brown and the centers spring back when lightly touched.
Remove the madeleines from the oven and allow them to cool slightly in the pan for a few minutes.
Then, gently remove them from the pan and let them cool completely on a wire rack.
To make the lemon glaze, in a small bowl, combine ¾ cups powdered sugar, 1 tablespoon of fresh lemon juice, and 2 tablespoons of water.
Stir until smooth.
If the glaze is too thick, add more lemon juice or water a teaspoon at a time until the desired consistency is reached.
Brush or drizzle the lemon glaze over the cooled madeleines.
Allow the glaze to set before serving the madeleines.
Enjoy your freshly baked Lemon Glazed Madeleines!

label: Fried Stuffed Olives
prep: In a small bowl, mix together the minced garlic, anchovy paste, grated lemon zest, chopped thyme, and chopped basil to create the filling.
Carefully pit the olives if not already pitted, ensuring they maintain their shape.
Using a small spoon or a piping bag, stuff each olive with the prepared filling.
Set up three shallow bowls for the breading process.
In the first bowl, place the flour.
In the second bowl, beat the eggs with 1 tablespoon of water to make an egg wash.
In the third bowl, place the seasoned bread crumbs.
Roll each stuffed olive in the flour to coat, shaking off any excess.
Dip next into the egg wash, and finally, roll them in the bread crumbs, ensuring they are well coated.
In a deep skillet or a frying pan, heat olive oil over medium-high heat.
The oil should be deep enough to submerge the olives, about 2 inches deep.
Once the oil is hot (about 350°F, or when a breadcrumb sizzles upon contact), fry the olives in batches, being careful not to overcrowd the pan.
Fry until they are golden and crispy, about 2-3 minutes.
Using a slotted spoon, transfer the fried olives to a plate lined with paper towels to drain excess oil.
Serve the fried stuffed olives hot, optionally with a side of marinara sauce or aioli for dipping.
Enjoy your crispy, savory treat!

label: Cheese Stuffed Shells
prep: Preheat your oven to 375°F.
Cook the pasta shells according to the package instructions until they are al dente.
Drain and set aside to cool.
In a large mixing bowl, combine the ricotta cheese, 1 cup of mozzarella cheese, Parmesan cheese, chopped parsley, oregano, basil, garlic salt, pepper, and eggs.
Mix well until all ingredients are thoroughly combined.
Spread about 1 cup of spaghetti sauce in the bottom of a 9x13 inch baking dish.
Take each cooked pasta shell and fill it with the cheese mixture using a spoon.
Arrange the filled shells in the baking dish over the layer of sauce.
Pour the remaining spaghetti sauce evenly over the stuffed shells.
Make sure all the shells are covered with sauce to prevent them from drying out during baking.
Sprinkle the remaining 1 cup of mozzarella cheese over the top of the sauce.
Cover the baking dish with aluminum foil and bake in the preheated oven for 25 minutes.
Remove the foil and continue baking for an additional 10-15 minutes, or until the cheese is bubbly and slightly golden.
Remove from the oven and let the dish rest for 5 minutes before serving.
Enjoy your delicious Cheese Stuffed Shells!

label: Turkey Meatloaf Muffins
prep: Preheat your oven to 375°F.
Lightly grease a 12-cup muffin tin or line with muffin liners.
In a large skillet over medium heat, sauté the chopped bell peppers, onions, and minced garlic until they are soft and slightly browned, about 5-7 minutes.
Set aside to cool slightly.
In a large mixing bowl, combine the ground turkey, breadcrumbs, and egg.
Add the cooled vegetable mixture to the bowl.
Pour in the Worcestershire sauce and chicken stock.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Mix all the ingredients together until well combined but avoid overmixing to keep the meatloaf tender.
Divide the turkey mixture evenly among the prepared muffin cups, pressing gently to fill them.
Place the muffin tin in the preheated oven and bake for 25-30 minutes, or until the meatloaf muffins are cooked through and the tops are slightly browned.
Remove the muffin tin from the oven and let the turkey meatloaf muffins cool in the pan for about 5 minutes before removing them.
Serve the turkey meatloaf muffins warm, optionally with a side of your favorite sauce or gravy.
Enjoy your meal!

label: Linguini With White Clam Sauce
prep: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil.
Add linguine and cook according to package instructions until al dente.
Drain and set aside, reserving 1 cup of pasta water.
While the pasta cooks, heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add the red pepper flakes and chopped garlic, sautéing until the garlic is fragrant but not browned, about 1-2 minutes.
Add the anchovy fillets to the skillet, breaking them up with a spoon until they dissolve into the oil.
Stir in the dried thyme and cook for another minute.
Increase the heat to medium-high and add the dry white wine and chicken stock.
Bring the mixture to a simmer and let it reduce by half, about 5-7 minutes.
Add the clams with their juice to the skillet.
Cover and cook until the clams are heated through, about 5 minutes.
Zest the lemon and squeeze its juice into the skillet.
Stir well to combine.
Add the cooked linguine to the skillet, tossing to coat with the clam sauce.
If the sauce is too thick, add some reserved pasta water to reach desired consistency.
Stir in the chopped parsley, and season with coarse salt and black pepper to taste.
Serve the linguini with white clam sauce hot, garnished with additional parsley and lemon zest if desired.
Accompany with slices of crusty bread for mopping up the delicious sauce.

label: Skirt Steak With Chimichurri Sauce
prep: Start by making the chimichurri sauce.
In a food processor, combine 1 cup of fresh parsley (leaves and tender stems), 3.5 cloves of garlic (peeled), and 2 tablespoons of fresh oregano.
Pulse until the herbs and garlic are finely chopped.
Transfer the herb mixture to a small bowl.
Stir in ½ cup of olive oil and 2 tablespoons of red wine vinegar.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Mix well to combine all the ingredients.
Set the chimichurri sauce aside to allow the flavors to meld.
Preheat your grill, grill pan, or skillet over high heat.
While the grill is heating, prepare the skirt steak.
Pat the steak dry with paper towels to ensure proper searing.
Season the skirt steak generously on both sides with salt and black pepper.
Place the skirt steak on the hot grill or pan.
Cook for about 3 to 4 minutes on each side for medium-rare, or adjust the cooking time according to your preferred level of doneness.
Once cooked to your liking, transfer the steak to a cutting board and let it rest for about 5 minutes.
This helps the juices redistribute throughout the meat, making it more tender and flavorful.
Slice the steak against the grain into thin strips.
This is crucial for ensuring the meat is tender and not chewy.
Serve the sliced skirt steak on a platter, drizzled with the chimichurri sauce or with the sauce on the side for dipping.
Enjoy your flavorful skirt steak with chimichurri sauce, perfect for a hearty meal with a vibrant touch!

label: Pineapple Mango Smoothie Bowl
prep: In a blender, combine 1 cup chopped pineapple, 1 cup mango, and 1 banana.
Add 1 cup coconut milk to the blender.
Blend on high until the mixture is smooth and creamy.
Pour the smoothie into a bowl.
Optionally, garnish with additional chopped pineapple, mango, or banana slices for added texture and flavor.
Serve immediately and enjoy your refreshing Pineapple Mango Smoothie Bowl!

label: Tagliatelle
prep: In a large mixing bowl, combine ¾ cup bread flour and ¾ cup semolina flour with a pinch of salt.
Mix well to distribute the salt evenly.
Make a well in the center of the flour mixture.
Crack 3 eggs (2 whole eggs and 1 additional egg) into the well.
Using a fork, gently beat the eggs, gradually incorporating the flour from the sides of the well.
Continue mixing until the dough begins to come together.
Once the dough is roughly combined, transfer it onto a clean, lightly floured surface.
Knead the dough for about 8 to 10 minutes, or until it becomes smooth and elastic.
Add a little more bread flour if the dough is too sticky.
Wrap the kneaded dough in plastic wrap and let it rest at room temperature for at least 30 minutes.
This allows the gluten to relax, making the dough easier to roll out.
After resting, divide the dough into 4 equal portions.
Work with one portion at a time, keeping the others covered to prevent drying out.
Flatten the dough portion into a rectangle shape.
Using a pasta machine or a rolling pin, roll the dough out into a thin sheet, about 1/16 inch thick.
If using a pasta machine, start at the widest setting and gradually reduce the setting with each pass.
Once the dough is rolled out thinly, use a sharp knife or a pasta cutter to cut it into tagliatelle strands, about ¼ inch wide.
Dust the cut pasta with a little semolina flour to prevent sticking and lay them out on a baking sheet or hang them on a pasta drying rack.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil.
Cook the tagliatelle in boiling water for 2 to 3 minutes, or until al dente.
Drain the pasta and serve with your favorite sauce.
Enjoy your homemade tagliatelle!

label: Fennel, Beet, And Orange Salad
prep: Preheat the oven to 400°F.
Trim the tops off the beets, scrub them clean, then wrap each beet individually in aluminum foil.
Place the wrapped beets on a baking sheet.
Roast the beets in the preheated oven until they are tender and can be easily pierced with a fork, about 45-60 minutes depending on their size.
Remove from the oven and let cool until they can be handled.
While the beets are cooling, prepare the fennel.
Trim the bottom of the fennel bulb and remove any tough or bruised outer layers.
Slice the fennel bulb very thinly using a mandoline or a sharp knife.
Peel the cooled beets.
The skins should slip off easily after roasting.
Slice the beets into thin rounds or wedges, as preferred.
Peel the oranges.
Using a sharp knife, cut between the membranes to segment the oranges, capturing the juice in a bowl.
Squeeze the remaining membrane over the bowl to extract all the juice.
In a small bowl, whisk together 2 tablespoons of the captured orange juice, 2 teaspoons of extra virgin olive oil, orange zest, sea salt, and pepper to taste to make the dressing.
Arrange the sliced fennel and beets on a serving platter.
Scatter the orange segments over the top.
Drizzle the dressing evenly over the salad.
Sprinkle with chopped fennel fronds.
In a separate small bowl, combine the remaining 1 tablespoon of orange juice and 1 teaspoon of olive oil.
Drizzle this mixture over the salad for added flavor and gloss.
Season with additional sea salt and pepper to taste.
Serve the salad chilled or at room temperature, allowing the flavors to meld together beautifully.
ingredientLines: 3 teaspoons extra virgin olive oil, divided

label: Heirloom Tomato And Goat Cheese Tart
prep: Preheat your oven to 375°F.
Roll out the pie crust and fit it into a 9-inch tart pan with a removable bottom.
Trim any excess crust and prick the bottom with a fork.
Chill in the refrigerator for about 15 minutes.
Line the chilled pie crust with parchment paper and fill with pie weights or dried beans.
Bake in the preheated oven for 20 minutes.
Remove the weights and parchment paper, and bake for an additional 5 minutes, or until the crust is lightly golden.
Remove from the oven and let cool slightly.
In a medium bowl, mix together the softened cream cheese and 4 ounces of softened goat cheese until smooth.
Spread this mixture evenly over the bottom of the cooled tart shell.
Slice the heirloom tomatoes into 1/4-inch thick slices.
Arrange the tomato slices over the cheese mixture in a single, overlapping layer.
Sprinkle the tomatoes with sea salt and ground black pepper.
Crumble the remaining ⅓ cup of goat cheese and sprinkle it over the tomatoes.
Bake the tart in the preheated oven for 25-30 minutes, or until the tomatoes are just starting to brown and the cheese is bubbly.
Remove the tart from the oven and let it cool for a few minutes.
Before serving, garnish with fresh oregano and basil leaves.
Serve warm or at room temperature, enjoying the blend of creamy cheeses and fresh, juicy tomatoes enhanced by the herbal freshness of the garnishes.

label: Irish Soda Bread Scones
prep: Preheat your oven to 400°F (200°C).
Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
In a large mixing bowl, whisk together the all-purpose flour, old-fashioned oats, sugar, baking powder, baking soda, and ¾ teaspoon salt.
Cut the unsalted butter into small pieces and add to the flour mixture.
Use a pastry cutter or your fingers to blend the butter into the flour until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs.
Stir in the dried cranberries and golden raisins.
In a separate bowl, whisk together the coconut cream, buttermilk, vanilla extract, and egg until well combined.
Make a well in the center of the dry ingredients and pour in the wet ingredients.
Gently fold everything together just until the dry ingredients are moistened.
Be careful not to overmix.
Turn the dough out onto a lightly floured surface.
Knead gently a few times just until the dough comes together.
Pat the dough into a round shape about 1 inch thick.
Use a sharp knife or a dough scraper to cut the dough into 8 wedges.
Place the wedges on the prepared baking sheet, spacing them slightly apart.
Sprinkle the tops with sea salt.
Bake in the preheated oven for 22-25 minutes, or until the scones are golden brown and a toothpick inserted into the center comes out clean.
Remove from the oven and let cool on the baking sheet for a few minutes, then transfer to a wire rack to cool completely.
Enjoy your Irish Soda Bread Scones warm or at room temperature, perhaps with a bit of butter or a drizzle of honey.

label: Vanilla Creme Brulee
prep: Preheat your oven to 325°F (163°C).
Arrange four ramekins in a deep baking dish and set aside.
In a medium saucepan, combine 1 cup of cream, 2½ fluid ounces of milk, and 1 vanilla pod (split lengthwise and seeds scraped).
Heat the mixture over medium heat until it just begins to simmer, then remove from heat.
Remove the vanilla pod but ensure to scrape any remaining seeds into the cream mixture.
In a mixing bowl, whisk together 4 egg yolks, 3 tablespoons of caster sugar, and 1 teaspoon of vanilla extract until the mixture is light and creamy.
Gradually pour the hot cream mixture into the egg yolk mixture, whisking constantly to prevent the eggs from scrambling.
Strain the mixture through a fine sieve into a clean bowl to remove any lumps and ensure a smooth custard.
Divide the custard evenly among the prepared ramekins.
Pour hot water into the baking dish until it comes halfway up the sides of the ramekins.
Carefully place the baking dish in the preheated oven and bake for about 30 to 35 minutes, or until the custards are just set but still slightly wobbly in the center.
Remove the ramekins from the water bath and allow them to cool to room temperature.
Once cooled, refrigerate the custards for at least 2 hours or up to 2 days.
When ready to serve, evenly sprinkle the remaining 3½ tablespoons of caster sugar over the custards.
Use a kitchen torch to caramelize the sugar until it forms a crispy top.
If you don't have a torch, you can place the ramekins under a broiler for a couple of minutes to achieve the caramelization.
Allow the crème brûlée to sit for a few minutes before serving to let the sugar harden into a delicious, crackly top.
Enjoy your homemade Vanilla Crème Brûlée!

label: Pepperoni Bread
prep: Preheat your oven to 375°F.
Line a baking sheet with parchment paper or lightly grease it.
On a lightly floured surface, roll out the thawed bread dough into a rectangle approximately 10x14 inches.
In a small bowl, beat the egg and brush a thin layer over the surface of the dough to help the toppings adhere.
Evenly distribute the sausage over the dough, leaving a small margin around the edges for sealing.
If the sausage is precooked, crumble it; if it's raw, remove it from the casing and crumble it as you spread it.
Sprinkle the shredded mozzarella cheese and grated Parmesan cheese over the sausage.
Then, evenly sprinkle the Italian seasoning across the cheese.
Starting from one long side, carefully roll the dough into a log, enclosing the fillings.
Pinch the seams and ends closed to seal all the ingredients inside.
Transfer the roll seam-side down to the prepared baking sheet.
Brush the top with the remaining beaten egg to give the bread a golden crust.
Bake in the preheated oven for 25 to 30 minutes, or until the bread is golden brown and sounds hollow when tapped.
Remove from the oven and let it cool slightly on a wire rack for about 5 minutes.
Slice the pepperoni bread into pieces and serve warm.
Enjoy your homemade pepperoni bread as a delicious snack or appetizer!

label: Coconut Jam Drops
prep: Preheat your oven to 350°F (175°C).
Line two baking sheets with parchment paper.
In a large mixing bowl, cream together 0.7 pounds of butter and 1 cup of caster sugar until light and fluffy.
Beat in 2 eggs and 2 teaspoons of vanilla essence until well combined.
In another bowl, sift together 2½ cups of maida (all-purpose flour) and ¾ teaspoon of baking powder.
Gradually add the dry ingredients to the wet ingredients, mixing until just combined.
Stir in 2 cups of shredded coconut into the dough until evenly distributed.
Roll the dough into small balls, about 1 inch in diameter, and place them on the prepared baking sheets, spacing them about 2 inches apart.
Make a small indentation in the center of each ball using your thumb or the back of a spoon.
Fill each indentation with a small amount of jam (about 1 teaspoon).
Bake in the preheated oven for 12-15 minutes, or until the edges are lightly golden.
Remove from the oven and allow to cool on the baking sheets for a few minutes before transferring to a wire rack to cool completely.
Enjoy your Coconut Jam Drops as a delightful treat with tea or as a sweet snack!

label: Jamaican Chicken
prep: Heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Season the chicken breasts with salt and black pepper.
Add the chicken to the skillet and cook until golden brown on both sides, about 5-7 minutes per side.
Remove the chicken from the skillet and set aside.
In the same skillet, add the chopped onion and sauté until translucent, about 3-4 minutes.
Add the finely chopped garlic, curry powder, ground allspice, and red pepper flakes to the onions.
Cook, stirring frequently, for about 1 minute until the spices are fragrant.
Stir in the diced tomatoes with their juice, black beans, and fresh thyme.
Bring the mixture to a simmer.
Return the chicken breasts to the skillet, nestling them into the sauce.
Cover and let simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until the chicken is cooked through and the flavors are well blended.
Adjust seasoning with additional salt and black pepper if needed.
Garnish with chopped cilantro before serving.
Enjoy your Jamaican Chicken, ideally served over rice or with a side of warm bread to soak up the delicious sauce.
ingredientLines: 12 ounces chicken breasts, boneless and skinless

label: Pasta With Vodka Sauce
prep: Begin by melting the butter in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add the finely chopped yellow onion and sauté until it becomes translucent, about 5 minutes.
Stir in the sliced garlic and a pinch of red pepper flakes, cooking until the garlic is fragrant, about 1 minute.
Season with kosher salt to taste.
Incorporate the tomato paste into the skillet, stirring continuously until the paste darkens slightly, about 5 minutes.
Pour in the vodka carefully and let it simmer until the alcohol is mostly evaporated, about 2 to 3 minutes.
Crush the whole, peeled tomatoes with your hands or a potato masher and add them to the skillet.
Bring the mixture to a simmer and let it cook for about 15 minutes, stirring occasionally.
While the sauce simmers, bring a large pot of salted water to a boil.
Cook the rigatoni according to the package instructions until al dente.
Drain and set aside.
Stir the heavy cream into the tomato sauce, mixing well until the sauce becomes creamy and smooth.
Allow it to simmer for an additional 5 minutes.
Add the cooked rigatoni to the sauce, tossing to coat the pasta evenly.
Remove the skillet from heat and stir in the grated Parmigiano-Reggiano cheese until melted and well incorporated.
Serve the pasta hot, garnished with additional Parmigiano-Reggiano if desired.

label: Butternut Squash Stuffing
prep: Preheat oven to 375°F.
Peel, seed, and dice the butternut squash into 1/2-inch cubes.
Dice the baguette into 1-inch cubes and set aside.
In a large skillet over medium heat, melt the butter.
Add the chopped celery, diced shallots, and chopped white onion.
Sauté until the vegetables are softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes.
Add the diced butternut squash to the skillet and cook, stirring occasionally, until the squash begins to soften, about 10 minutes.
Stir in the chicken broth, chopped fresh sage, kosher salt, black pepper, and crushed red pepper.
Bring the mixture to a simmer and cook for another 5 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld.
In a large mixing bowl, combine the sautéed vegetable and squash mixture with the cubed baguette.
Toss well to ensure the bread absorbs the broth and the mixture is evenly combined.
Transfer the stuffing mixture to a greased 9x13-inch baking dish.
Cover the dish with aluminum foil.
Bake in the preheated oven for 25 minutes.
Remove the foil and continue baking for an additional 20-25 minutes, or until the top is golden brown and crispy.
Remove from the oven and let it cool slightly before serving.
Enjoy your Butternut Squash Stuffing as a hearty side dish!

label: Carrot Ginger Pumpkin Soup
prep: Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Chop the onion and ginger root finely, then add them to the pot.
Cook until the onions become translucent, about 5 minutes.
Add the minced garlic to the pot and cook for another minute until fragrant.
Peel and slice the carrots into rounds, then add them to the pot.
Stir to combine with the onion, ginger, and garlic.
Pour in the vegetable broth and bring the mixture to a boil.
Once boiling, reduce the heat to low and simmer until the carrots are tender, about 20 minutes.
Stir in the pumpkin puree and a pinch of curry powder.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Continue to simmer for another 10 minutes to let the flavors meld.
Use an immersion blender to puree the soup directly in the pot until smooth.
Alternatively, you can transfer the soup in batches to a blender and blend until smooth, then return it to the pot.
Taste and adjust seasoning if necessary.
If the soup is too thick, add a bit more vegetable broth to reach your desired consistency.
Serve the soup hot, garnished with a drizzle of olive oil or a sprinkle of curry powder if desired.

label: Sticky Rice
prep: Rinse the rice under cold water until the water runs clear.
This helps to remove excess starch and prevent the rice from becoming too sticky.
In a medium pot, bring 1 pint of water to a boil.
Add the rinsed rice and a pinch of salt, then stir.
Reduce the heat to low, cover the pot, and let the rice simmer for 18-20 minutes, or until the water is absorbed and the rice is tender.
While the rice is cooking, prepare the chicken.
Cut the ½ chicken into smaller pieces.
Peel and finely chop the onion.
In a skillet, heat a tablespoon of oil over medium heat.
Add the chopped onion and sauté until translucent and slightly golden, about 5-7 minutes.
Add the chicken pieces to the skillet with the onion.
Cook until the chicken is browned on all sides and cooked through, about 10-15 minutes, depending on the size of the pieces.
Once the rice is cooked, remove it from the heat and let it sit, still covered, for 5 minutes.
Then, fluff it with a fork to separate the grains.
Chop the bunch of parsley finely.
Mix the cooked chicken and onions into the pot of rice, combining them thoroughly.
Sprinkle the chopped parsley over the mixture and stir to distribute evenly.
Serve the sticky rice hot, garnished with additional parsley if desired.

label: Peanut Butter Icing
prep: In a medium mixing bowl, combine ½ cup powdered sugar and 2 tablespoons peanut butter.
Gradually add 1 tablespoon of milk to the mixture, stirring continuously until the icing is smooth and well combined.
If the icing is too thick, add a little more milk, a few drops at a time, until you reach the desired consistency.
Use immediately to frost cakes, cupcakes, or other desserts, or store in an airtight container in the refrigerator until needed.
Stir well before using if stored.

label: Maple Walnut Ice Cream
prep: In a medium saucepan, combine heavy cream, buttermilk, and 3/4 cup maple syrup.
Heat over medium heat until the mixture is warm and begins to steam, but do not let it boil.
In a separate bowl, whisk together the egg yolks and salt until smooth.
Gradually temper the egg yolks by adding a small amount of the warm cream mixture to the yolks, whisking constantly.
Continue adding the warm cream mixture slowly to the yolks until about half of the cream mixture has been incorporated.
Pour the tempered yolk mixture back into the saucepan with the remaining cream mixture.
Cook over low heat, stirring constantly, until the mixture thickens enough to coat the back of a spoon, about 5 to 7 minutes.
Remove the saucepan from heat and strain the custard through a fine-mesh sieve into a clean bowl.
Stir in the remaining 1/4 cup maple syrup.
Cover and chill the custard in the refrigerator until completely cold, about 2 to 3 hours.
While the custard is chilling, preheat the oven to 350°F.
Spread the walnuts on a baking sheet and toast in the oven until they are golden and fragrant, about 8 to 10 minutes.
Allow the walnuts to cool, then roughly chop them.
Once the custard is chilled, pour it into an ice cream maker and churn according to the manufacturer's instructions until it reaches the consistency of soft serve.
In the last few minutes of churning, add the chopped toasted walnuts to the ice cream maker, allowing them to mix thoroughly into the ice cream.
Transfer the ice cream to an airtight container and freeze until firm, about 2 to 4 hours, before serving.

label: Arugula Basil Pesto
prep: In a food processor, combine the arugula, basil, pine nuts, Parmesan cheese, and garlic.
Pulse a few times to chop and blend the ingredients.
With the processor running, slowly pour in the olive oil through the feed tube.
Continue to process until the mixture forms a smooth paste.
Taste and adjust seasoning, adding more Parmesan or olive oil if needed to achieve desired consistency and flavor.
Use immediately or store in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to a week.

label: Curry Lentil Soup
prep: Rinse the lentils under cold water until the water runs clear.
Set aside to drain.
Peel and finely chop the onion and garlic.
In a large pot, heat the olive oil over medium heat.
Add the chopped onion and garlic, sautéing until the onion becomes translucent, about 5 minutes.
Stir in the curry powder and cook for another minute until the spices are fragrant.
Add the rinsed lentils to the pot along with the vegetable broth.
Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat to low and simmer, covered, for about 20-25 minutes, or until the lentils are tender.
Stir in the coconut milk and continue to simmer for another 5 minutes.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Remove from heat and add a squeeze of fresh lemon juice.
Adjust seasoning if necessary.
Serve hot, garnished with chopped parsley.

label: Antipasto Tortellini Pasta Salad
prep: Cook the tortellini according to package instructions until al dente.
Drain and rinse under cold water to cool.
Set aside in a large mixing bowl.
While the tortellini is cooking, prepare the dressing.
In a small bowl, whisk together the olive oil, red wine vinegar, minced garlic, dried oregano, red pepper flakes, and a pinch of kosher salt.
Adjust the seasoning to taste and set aside.

To the bowl with the cooled tortellini, add the cherry tomatoes, mixed olives, chopped pepperoni, chopped sopressata, mozzarella balls, provolone cheese (cut into small cubes), sliced roasted red peppers, thinly sliced red onion, and pepperoncini peppers.
Pour the dressing over the salad and toss gently to combine all the ingredients well and ensure everything is evenly coated with the dressing.
Tear the fresh basil leaves by hand and sprinkle them over the salad.
Give the salad a final gentle mix.
Cover the bowl with plastic wrap and refrigerate for at least 1 hour to allow the flavors to meld together.
Before serving, give the salad a quick toss to redistribute the dressing and ingredients.
Serve chilled or at room temperature.
Enjoy your Antipasto Tortellini Pasta Salad as a vibrant and flavorful side dish or a main course on a warm day.
ingredientLines: ¾ cups roasted red peppers, sliced

ingredients.text: ¾ cups roasted red peppers, sliced

label: Swiss Chard With Raisins And Pine Nuts
prep: Rinse the Swiss chard thoroughly under cold water.
Trim off the ends of the stems and chop the leaves into large pieces.
Set aside.
In a large skillet, heat the olive oil over medium heat.
Add the chopped onions and sauté until they become translucent and slightly golden, about 5 to 7 minutes.
Add the Swiss chard to the skillet.
Cook, stirring occasionally, until the leaves wilt and reduce in volume, about 5 minutes.
Stir in the balsamic vinegar and golden raisins.
Continue to cook for another 2 to 3 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld together and the vinegar to slightly reduce.
Sprinkle the roasted pine nuts over the chard.
Toss everything together gently to distribute the nuts and raisins evenly.
Serve warm as a side dish, ensuring each serving is garnished with some of the pine nuts and raisins.

label: Refried Black Beans
prep: Heat the vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Drain and rinse one can of black beans.
Add these beans to the skillet.
Mash the beans coarsely with a potato masher or the back of a fork.
Stir in the green chilies and ground cumin, cooking for about 2 minutes to blend the flavors.
Drain and rinse the second can of black beans and add them to the skillet.
Stir well to combine.
Cook the mixture, stirring occasionally, until the beans are heated through and begin to thicken, about 5 to 7 minutes.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Serve hot as a side dish or use as a filling for tacos or burritos.

label: Mussels Mariniere
prep: Clean the mussels by scrubbing them under cold water.
Remove the beards (the fibrous tufts sticking out from the shells) and discard any mussels that are open and do not close when tapped.
Finely chop the onion and carrot.
Mince the garlic if not already minced.
In a large pot, melt the butter over medium heat.
Add the chopped onion and carrot, and cook until the onion is translucent, about 5 minutes.
Add the minced garlic to the pot and cook for another minute until fragrant.
Pour in the dry vermouth and add the bay leaf, thyme, and tarragon sprigs to the pot.
Bring the mixture to a simmer.
Add the cleaned mussels to the pot.
Cover with a lid and let the mussels steam for about 5 to 7 minutes, or until they open.
Shake the pot occasionally to ensure even cooking.
Discard any mussels that do not open after cooking.
Using a slotted spoon, transfer the opened mussels to serving bowls.
Stir the chopped parsley into the broth in the pot, then taste and adjust seasoning if necessary.
Ladle the broth over the mussels in the bowls.
Serve hot, ideally with crusty bread to soak up the flavorful broth.

label: Spaghetti With Mushrooms
prep: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil.
Add the whole wheat spaghetti and cook according to the package instructions until al dente.
Drain and set aside, reserving 1 cup of pasta water.
While the pasta is cooking, clean the Portobello mushrooms with a damp cloth and slice them.
Dice the vine tomatoes, mince the shallots, and finely chop the garlic.
Heat 3 tablespoons of olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add the shallots and garlic, sautéing until they become translucent and fragrant, about 2-3 minutes.
Add the sliced mushrooms to the skillet.
Cook, stirring occasionally, until the mushrooms are golden and tender, about 5-7 minutes.
Stir in the diced tomatoes and cook for another 3-4 minutes, until the tomatoes start to break down.
Tear the basil leaves and add them to the skillet.
Season the mixture with salt and pepper to taste.
Reduce the heat to low.
Add the cooked spaghetti to the skillet.
Toss well to combine with the mushroom and tomato mixture.
If the mixture seems dry, add a bit of the reserved pasta water to moisten.
Drizzle the remaining 3 tablespoons of olive oil over the pasta and toss again to coat evenly.
Grate the Parmesan cheese over the top of the spaghetti.
Serve the spaghetti hot, with additional Parmesan cheese on the side if desired.

label: Garlic Oven Fries
prep: Preheat your oven to 425°F.
Line a large baking sheet with parchment paper for easy cleanup.
Wash and peel the russet potatoes.
Cut them into sticks approximately 1/4 inch wide and 3 inches long to create evenly sized fries.
Place the cut potatoes in a large bowl and cover them with cold water.
Let them soak for at least 30 minutes to remove excess starch, which helps in achieving crispier fries.
Drain the potatoes and pat them dry thoroughly with a clean kitchen towel or paper towels.
In a large bowl, combine the dried potato sticks with 2 tablespoons of olive oil and ½ teaspoon of sea salt.
Toss until the potatoes are evenly coated.
Spread the potatoes in a single layer on the prepared baking sheet, ensuring they aren't overcrowded to allow for even cooking.
Bake in the preheated oven for 15 minutes.
Meanwhile, crush the 3 cloves of garlic.
Remove the baking sheet from the oven and sprinkle the crushed garlic evenly over the fries.
Toss the fries gently to distribute the garlic.
Return the baking sheet to the oven and continue to bake for another 15-20 minutes, or until the fries are golden brown and crispy.
Remove from the oven and let the garlic oven fries cool slightly on the baking sheet for a few minutes before serving.
This allows them to crisp up further.
Enjoy your crispy and flavorful garlic oven fries as a delicious side dish or snack!

label: Buffalo Chicken Nachos
prep: Preheat your oven to 375°F.
Line a baking sheet with aluminum foil and lightly grease it with cooking spray or a bit of oil.
Place the chicken breasts and the whole onion (peeled) in a medium saucepan.
Cover with water and bring to a boil over medium-high heat.
Reduce the heat to a simmer and cook until the chicken is fully cooked, about 15-20 minutes.
While the chicken is cooking, prepare the buffalo sauce.
In a small bowl, combine the hot sauce and melted butter.
Stir well to mix.
Once the chicken is cooked, remove it from the water and let it cool slightly.
Using two forks, shred the chicken into bite-sized pieces.
Transfer the shredded chicken to a large mixing bowl.
Pour the buffalo sauce over the chicken and toss to coat evenly.
Spread the tortilla chips in an even layer on the prepared baking sheet.
Evenly distribute the buffalo chicken over the chips.
Sprinkle the cheddar cheese over the chicken and chips.
Chop the boiled onion and scatter it over the cheese.
Bake in the preheated oven until the cheese is melted and bubbly, about 10-15 minutes.
While the nachos are baking, slice the scallions and chop the cherry tomatoes.
Remove the nachos from the oven.
Drizzle blue cheese dressing over the top, then sprinkle with chopped scallions and cherry tomatoes.
Serve immediately, enjoying the spicy, cheesy, and crunchy combination of your Buffalo Chicken Nachos.
ingredientLines: ½ cup blue cheese salad dressing

ingredients.text: ½ cup blue cheese salad dressing

label: Beef And Butternut Squash Stew
prep: Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add the chopped onion and garlic, and sauté until the onion becomes translucent, about 5 minutes.
Stir in the minced rosemary and chopped thyme, cooking for another minute until fragrant.
Season the beef with salt and black pepper.
Add the beef to the pot and cook until browned on all sides, about 6-8 minutes.
Sprinkle the all-purpose flour over the beef and stir to coat the pieces evenly.
Cook for another 2 minutes to remove the raw flour taste.
Pour in the wine, scraping any browned bits off the bottom of the pot with a wooden spoon.
Allow the wine to simmer and reduce slightly, about 3 minutes.
Add the cubed butternut squash and chopped sun-dried tomatoes to the pot.
Stir to combine.
Pour in the beef broth and bring the mixture to a boil.
Once boiling, reduce the heat to low and cover the pot.
Let the stew simmer gently for about 1 hour, or until the beef is tender and the squash is cooked through.
Remove the lid and increase the heat to medium.
Allow the stew to simmer uncovered for another 10-15 minutes to thicken slightly.
Stir in the chopped fresh parsley and adjust seasoning with additional salt and pepper if needed.
Serve the beef and butternut squash stew hot with a side of bread for dipping into the flavorful broth.

label: Magic Bars
prep: Preheat your oven to 350°F (175°C).
Line a 9x13-inch baking pan with parchment paper, allowing the paper to overhang the edges for easy removal later.
In a medium bowl, combine the 1½ cups cracker crumbs with the ½ cup melted butter.
Mix well until the crumbs are evenly moistened.
Press the crumb mixture firmly into the bottom of the prepared baking pan to form a solid, even layer.
This will be the crust for your magic bars.
Sprinkle the 1 cup chopped walnuts evenly over the crumb crust.
Layer the 1½ cups semisweet chocolate chips next, spreading them evenly across the walnuts.
Follow with a layer of 1½ cups flaked coconut, distributing it evenly over the chocolate chips.
Drizzle the 1⅓ cups sweetened condensed milk evenly over the entire layer of coconut.
Make sure to cover as much of the surface as possible, as this will help bind all the layers together upon baking.
Place the pan in the preheated oven and bake for 25 to 30 minutes, or until the top is lightly browned and the edges are bubbly.
Remove the pan from the oven and allow the bars to cool completely in the pan on a wire rack.
Once cooled, use the overhanging parchment paper to lift the bars out of the pan.
Cut into squares or bars of your desired size and serve.
Enjoy your delicious homemade magic bars!

label: Mango Salsa Chicken
prep: Preheat your grill or a grill pan over medium-high heat.
In a small bowl, mix together the brown sugar, chili powder, and garlic powder.
Rub this mixture all over the chicken breasts.
Lightly oil the grill or grill pan.
Place the chicken on the grill and cook for about 6-7 minutes on each side, or until the chicken is thoroughly cooked and has an internal temperature of 165°F.
While the chicken is cooking, peel and dice the mango and avocado.
Place them in a medium bowl.
Add the chopped red onion, chopped cilantro, and vinaigrette to the bowl with the mango and avocado.
Gently toss to combine all the ingredients.
Once the chicken is cooked, remove it from the grill and let it rest for a few minutes.
Slice the chicken into strips or cubes, as preferred.
Serve the grilled chicken topped with the mango avocado salsa.
Enjoy your Mango Salsa Chicken fresh and full of flavor!
ingredientLines: 1 pound boneless skinless chicken breast, large

ingredients.text: 1 pound boneless skinless chicken breast, large

label: Cinnamon Sugar Muffins
prep: Preheat your oven to 350°F (175°C).
Grease a 12-cup muffin tin or line with paper muffin liners.
In a large bowl, whisk together the flour, baking powder, salt, and nutmeg.
Set aside.
In another bowl, whisk together the olive oil and granulated sugar until well combined.
Beat in the egg until the mixture is smooth.
Gradually add the milk to the sugar and egg mixture, stirring continuously until everything is well incorporated.
Add the wet ingredients to the dry ingredients, stirring just until the flour is moistened.
Be careful not to overmix.
Fold in the raisins gently.
Spoon the batter into the prepared muffin tin, filling each cup about two-thirds full.
Bake in the preheated oven for 20-25 minutes, or until a toothpick inserted into the center of a muffin comes out clean.
While the muffins are baking, prepare a small bowl with the melted butter and another small bowl with the cinnamon sugar.
Once the muffins are done, remove them from the oven and let them cool for a few minutes in the pan.
Then, while still warm, dip the top of each muffin first into the melted butter and then into the cinnamon sugar to coat.
Serve the muffins warm or at room temperature.
Enjoy your delicious Cinnamon Sugar Muffins!

label: Pasta Pomodoro
prep: Begin by heating the olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add the finely chopped yellow onion and sauté until it becomes translucent, about 5 minutes.
Add the minced garlic and crushed red pepper flakes to the skillet.
Cook for an additional 1-2 minutes, or until the garlic is fragrant but not browned.
Crush the whole, peeled tomatoes with your hands or a potato masher and add them to the skillet.
Stir in the kosher salt.
Bring the mixture to a simmer and let it cook for about 15-20 minutes, or until the sauce thickens slightly.
While the sauce is simmering, bring a large pot of salted water to a boil.
Add the spaghetti and cook according to the package instructions until al dente.
Drain the pasta, reserving about 1 cup of the pasta water.
Once the tomato sauce has thickened, reduce the heat to low and stir in the chopped basil and unsalted butter.
Mix until the butter is fully incorporated.
Add the cooked spaghetti directly to the sauce.
Toss well to coat the pasta in the sauce, adding a little reserved pasta water if needed to help the sauce cling to the pasta.
Remove the skillet from the heat and stir in the grated Parmesan cheese.
Mix until the cheese is melted and the pasta is evenly coated.
Serve the Pasta Pomodoro hot, garnished with additional basil and Parmesan cheese sprinkled on top.
Enjoy your meal!
ingredientLines: ¼ teaspoon red pepper flakes, crushed

ingredients.text: ¼ teaspoon red pepper flakes, crushed

label: Banana Bars With Cream Cheese Frosting
prep: Preheat your oven to 350°F (175°C).
Grease and flour a 9x13 inch baking pan; set aside.
In a large mixing bowl, cream together ½ cup softened butter and 1½ cups sugar until light and fluffy.
Beat in the eggs, one at a time, then stir in ½ cup low fat plain yogurt, ½ cup light sour cream, and 1 teaspoon vanilla extract until well combined.
In a separate bowl, whisk together 2 cups all-purpose flour, 1 teaspoon baking soda, and ¼ teaspoon salt.
Gradually add the dry ingredients to the wet ingredients, mixing until just incorporated.
Mash the bananas with a fork or potato masher until smooth.
Fold the mashed bananas into the batter.
Spread the batter evenly into the prepared baking pan.
Bake in the preheated oven for 25-30 minutes, or until a toothpick inserted into the center comes out clean.
Allow to cool completely in the pan on a wire rack.
While the bars are cooling, prepare the cream cheese frosting.
In a medium bowl, beat together 8 ounces softened cream cheese, ½ cup softened butter, and 2 teaspoons vanilla extract until smooth and creamy.
Gradually beat in 4 cups confectioners' sugar until the frosting is smooth and spreadable.
Once the bars are completely cooled, spread the cream cheese frosting evenly over the top.
Cut into bars and serve.
Optionally, you can refrigerate the bars for about an hour before serving to allow the frosting to set slightly, making them easier to cut and serve.
ingredientLines: ½ cup Low Fat Plain Yogurt

ingredients.text: ½ cup Low Fat Plain Yogurt

label: Duck Fat Roasted Potatoes
prep: Preheat your oven to 400°F (200°C).
Peel the potatoes and cut them into even-sized chunks, about 1.5 to 2 inches each.
Place the potatoes in a large pot and cover them with cold water.
Add a generous pinch of salt.
Bring the water to a boil over high heat, then reduce the heat to medium and simmer the potatoes for about 10 minutes, just until they start to become tender but are not fully cooked.
Drain the potatoes well in a colander and let them steam dry for a few minutes.
Shake the colander gently to fluff the edges of the potatoes, which will help to make them crispier when roasted.
In a roasting pan, melt the duck fat over medium heat on the stovetop until it is hot but not smoking.
Carefully add the potatoes to the hot fat, turning them to coat evenly.
Season generously with salt.
Transfer the roasting pan to the preheated oven and roast the potatoes for about 45-50 minutes, turning them occasionally, until they are golden brown and crisp all over.
Remove the potatoes from the oven and transfer them to a serving dish with a slotted spoon to drain any excess fat.
Serve hot, sprinkled with a little more salt if desired.

label: Coconut Fried Shrimp
prep: Heat oil in a deep fryer or large skillet to 350°F.
In a shallow bowl, combine flour, curry powder, salt, and pepper to taste.
In another shallow bowl, beat the eggs.
Place the shredded coconut in a third shallow bowl.
Pat the shrimp dry with paper towels.
Dredge each shrimp in the flour mixture, shaking off any excess.
Dip the floured shrimp into the beaten eggs, allowing any excess to drip off.
Coat the shrimp thoroughly in the shredded coconut, pressing gently to adhere.
Fry the shrimp in batches in the hot oil until golden brown and cooked through, about 2 to 3 minutes per side.
Do not overcrowd the pan.
Remove the shrimp with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels.
Serve hot with your choice of dipping sauce.

label: Shrimp Scampi Linguine
prep: Bring a large pot of water to a boil.
Add 1 teaspoon kosher salt and the linguine.
Cook according to package instructions until al dente.
Drain and set aside, reserving 1 cup of pasta water.
In a large skillet, heat the olive oil and 2 tablespoons of unsalted butter over medium heat.
Once the butter has melted, add the minced garlic and sauté for about 1 minute until fragrant but not browned.
Increase the heat to medium-high and add the shrimp to the skillet.
Season with the remaining ½ teaspoon kosher salt, ¼ teaspoon ground black pepper, and ¼ teaspoon crushed red pepper flakes.
Cook the shrimp for about 2 minutes on each side or until they turn pink and are just cooked through.
Remove the shrimp from the skillet and set aside.
In the same skillet, add the lemon juice from the 2 squeezed lemons and ¼ cup of the reserved pasta water.
Bring to a simmer, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan.
Return the shrimp to the skillet along with the cooked linguine.
Toss well to coat the pasta and shrimp with the sauce, adding more pasta water if needed to loosen the sauce.
Stir in the remaining 1 tablespoon of butter until melted and the sauce is creamy.
Remove from heat and stir in the chopped parsley.
Adjust seasoning with additional salt and pepper if needed.
Serve the shrimp scampi linguine garnished with lemon zest from the ¼ lemon and additional chopped parsley.
Optionally, you can add a squeeze of lemon juice for extra freshness right before serving.
ingredientLines: ¼ teaspoon red pepper flakes, crushed

ingredients.text: ¼ teaspoon red pepper flakes, crushed

label: Whole Wheat Carrot Muffins
prep: Preheat your oven to 375°F (190°C).
Line a muffin tin with paper liners or grease the cups lightly with oil or butter.
In a large mixing bowl, whisk together the whole wheat flour, baking powder, baking soda, salt, 2 teaspoons cinnamon, nutmeg, ginger, and allspice.
In another bowl, beat the eggs lightly.
Add the vegetable oil, 1¾ cups brown sugar, and Greek yogurt, mixing until well combined.
Stir the wet ingredients into the dry ingredients until just combined.
Be careful not to overmix.
Fold in the grated carrots and raisins gently into the batter.
In a small bowl, mix together ⅓ cup brown sugar, 1½ tablespoons all-purpose flour, ¼ teaspoon cinnamon, and 1 tablespoon unsalted butter.
Use a fork or your fingers to blend the ingredients until the mixture becomes crumbly.
This will be your streusel topping.
Spoon the batter into the prepared muffin tin, filling each cup about three-quarters full.
Sprinkle the streusel topping evenly over each muffin.
Bake in the preheated oven for 20-25 minutes, or until a toothpick inserted into the center of a muffin comes out clean.
Allow the muffins to cool in the pan for 5 minutes, then transfer them to a wire rack to cool completely.
Enjoy your whole wheat carrot muffins as a delightful breakfast or a healthy snack!

label: Crock Pot Chicken And Rice Soup
prep: Place the chicken breasts at the bottom of the crock pot.
Add the sliced mushrooms, celery, carrot, and chopped onion over the chicken.
Sprinkle the ground sage and pepper evenly over the vegetables and chicken.
Pour the chicken broth into the crock pot, ensuring that the ingredients are well-covered.
Cover the crock pot and cook on low for 6 hours or on high for 3 hours.
After the cooking time, remove the chicken breasts and shred them using two forks.
Return the shredded chicken to the crock pot.
Stir in the rice and mixed frozen vegetables.
Cover and continue to cook on high for an additional 45 minutes, or until the rice is tender and the vegetables are heated through.
Taste and adjust seasoning if necessary.
Serve hot, garnished with fresh herbs if desired.
ingredientLines: 1 cup frozen vegetables, fresh, blanched, mixed

ingredients.text: 1 cup frozen vegetables, fresh, blanched, mixed

label: Thai Steak Salad
prep: In a small bowl, whisk together lime juice, soy sauce, fish sauce, sugar, and minced garlic to create the dressing.
Set aside.
Season the sirloin steak with kosher salt and black pepper.
Heat vegetable oil in a skillet over medium-high heat.
Once hot, add the steak and cook for about 4-5 minutes on each side for medium-rare, or until it reaches your desired level of doneness.
Remove the steak from the skillet and let it rest for 5 minutes.
After resting, thinly slice the steak against the grain.
Wash and dry the Bibb lettuce, then tear the leaves into bite-sized pieces.
Place them in a large salad bowl.
Peel and julienne the carrots, and thinly slice the red bell pepper.
Trim the ends off the sugar snap peas and slice them diagonally.
Add the carrots, red bell pepper, and sugar snap peas to the salad bowl with the lettuce.
Add the sliced steak to the salad bowl.
Drizzle the prepared dressing over the salad and toss gently to combine.
Garnish the salad with shredded fresh mint and sliced jalapeños.
Serve the Thai Steak Salad immediately, offering extra dressing on the side if desired.

label: Grilled Salmon Steaks
prep: Preheat your grill to medium-high heat and lightly oil the grate with canola oil to prevent sticking.
In a small dry skillet, toast the cumin seeds, coriander seeds, fennel seeds, and green peppercorns over medium heat until they start to pop and release their aromas, about 1 to 2 minutes.
Be careful not to burn them.
Transfer the toasted spices to a mortar and pestle or a spice grinder.
Grind them into a coarse powder.
Season the salmon steaks generously with the ground spice mixture and sea salt, ensuring both sides are well-coated.
Place the salmon steaks on the preheated grill.
Cook for about 4 to 5 minutes on each side, or until the salmon is opaque and flakes easily with a fork.
The actual cooking time may vary depending on the thickness of the steaks.
Remove the salmon steaks from the grill and let them rest for a few minutes before serving to allow the juices to redistribute.
Serve the grilled salmon steaks hot, optionally garnished with a wedge of lemon or a sprinkle of fresh herbs for added flavor.

label: Creole Shrimp And Rice
prep: In a medium saucepan, bring 1½ cups of water to a boil.
Add the rice, reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 18-20 minutes or until the water is absorbed and the rice is tender.
Remove from heat and keep covered.
While the rice is cooking, heat 1 teaspoon of canola oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Season the shrimp with 1½ teaspoons of Creole seasoning.
Add the shrimp to the skillet and cook for about 2-3 minutes on each side, or until the shrimp are pink and cooked through.
Remove the shrimp from the skillet and set aside.
In the same skillet, add the remaining 2 teaspoons of canola oil.
Add the chopped onion and bell pepper, and sauté for about 5 minutes until the vegetables are softened.
Stir in the chopped thyme and minced garlic, and cook for an additional 1 minute until fragrant.
Sprinkle the flour over the vegetables and stir to coat.
Slowly pour in the milk while continuously stirring to create a smooth sauce.
Cook for 2-3 minutes until the sauce thickens slightly.
Chop the tomato and add it to the skillet.
Season the sauce with salt and pepper to taste.
Cook for another 2 minutes, allowing the tomato to soften and release its juices, enhancing the flavors of the sauce.
Return the cooked shrimp to the skillet and stir to combine.
Cook for another 2 minutes to reheat the shrimp and mingle the flavors.
Fluff the cooked rice with a fork and serve it as a bed in individual plates or a large serving dish.
Spoon the Creole shrimp and sauce over the rice.
Garnish with minced chives.
Serve hot and enjoy your Creole Shrimp and Rice, bursting with flavors and vibrant colors.

label: Veg Spring Roll
prep: Begin by making the spring roll wrappers.
In a mixing bowl, combine 8 tablespoons of all-purpose flour, 4 tablespoons of corn flour, and 2 pinches of salt.
Gradually add 1½ cups of water, whisking continuously to form a smooth, thin batter.
Heat a non-stick skillet over medium heat.
Pour a small amount of batter into the skillet, tilting it to spread the batter thinly over the surface.
Cook until the edges start to peel away from the skillet and the bottom is lightly browned, about 1-2 minutes.
Flip and cook for another 30 seconds.
Remove and place on a plate.
Repeat with the remaining batter to make more wrappers.
Set aside.
For the filling, heat 2 tablespoons of refined oil in a pan over medium heat.
Add ½ cup sliced onions, ½ cup sliced carrots, ½ cup sliced cabbage, and 1 sliced pepper capsicum.
Stir-fry the vegetables for about 2-3 minutes until they are just softened.
Add 2 teaspoons of soy sauce, 3 pinches of salt, 2 pinches of black pepper, and grated ginger to the vegetables.
Cook for another minute until everything is well combined and the vegetables are coated with the seasoning.
Turn off the heat and stir in the chopped coriander leaves.
To assemble the spring rolls, place a spring roll wrapper on a clean surface.
Spoon some of the vegetable mixture onto one edge of the wrapper.
Fold in the sides and roll the wrapper tightly around the filling, securing the end with a little paste made by mixing 3 tablespoons of all-purpose flour with water to create a glue-like consistency.
Heat oil in a deep fryer or a large pan to 350°F (175°C).
Carefully place the spring rolls in the hot oil and fry until golden brown and crispy, about 2-3 minutes.
Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels.
Serve the veg spring rolls hot with a dipping sauce of your choice, such as sweet chili sauce or more soy sauce.
Enjoy your crispy, homemade veg spring rolls!

label: Cinnamon Almond Butter
prep: Preheat your oven to 350°F.
Spread the almonds in a single layer on a baking sheet.
Toast the almonds in the oven for 10-12 minutes, stirring occasionally, until they are lightly browned and fragrant.
Remove from the oven and let cool slightly.
Transfer the toasted almonds to a food processor.
Process on high speed for about 10 minutes, scraping down the sides as needed, until the almonds break down into a smooth, creamy butter.
Once the almonds have transformed into butter, add the white sugar, brown sugar, ground cinnamon, and salt to the food processor.
Continue to process for another 2-3 minutes until all the ingredients are well incorporated and the mixture is smooth.
Transfer the cinnamon almond butter to an airtight container.
It can be stored at room temperature for a few days or refrigerated for up to a month.
Enjoy your homemade cinnamon almond butter spread on toast, mixed into oatmeal, or as a dip for fresh fruit.

label: Teriyaki Pork Tenderloin
prep: In a small bowl, combine the soy sauce, olive oil, minced garlic, brown sugar, ground ginger, black pepper, and honey.
Stir well to create the teriyaki marinade.
Place the pork tenderloin in a resealable plastic bag or a shallow dish.
Pour the marinade over the pork, ensuring it is well coated.
Seal the bag or cover the dish and refrigerate for at least 2 hours, or overnight for deeper flavor.
Preheat your oven to 375°F (190°C).
Remove the pork tenderloin from the marinade, reserving the marinade for basting.
Place the pork in a baking dish.
Bake in the preheated oven for 25-30 minutes, or until the pork reaches an internal temperature of 145°F (63°C).
Baste the pork occasionally with the reserved marinade during cooking.
Once cooked, remove the pork tenderloin from the oven and let it rest for 5 minutes before slicing.
This allows the juices to redistribute throughout the meat, making it more tender and flavorful.
Slice the pork tenderloin and serve with a drizzle of the cooked marinade as a sauce, if desired.
Enjoy your flavorful teriyaki pork tenderloin!

label: Churro Waffles
prep: Preheat your waffle iron according to the manufacturer's instructions.
In a large mixing bowl, whisk together the flour, ⅓ cup sugar, baking powder, and ½ teaspoon salt.
In another bowl, beat the eggs and then mix in the milk and oil until well combined.
Pour the wet ingredients into the dry ingredients and stir until just combined.
Be careful not to overmix; a few lumps are okay.
In a shallow dish, combine 1 cup sugar and ¼ cup cinnamon to make the cinnamon sugar.
Set aside.
Grease the preheated waffle iron with a little oil or non-stick spray.
Pour enough batter into the iron to just cover the waffle grid.
Close the waffle iron and cook according to the manufacturer's instructions until the waffle is golden and crisp.
Once each waffle is done, immediately brush both sides with melted butter and then dip each side into the cinnamon sugar mixture, coating it completely.
Serve the churro waffles warm, optionally with syrup, whipped cream, or your favorite toppings.
Enjoy the delightful blend of crispy waffle and sweet, spiced sugar!

label: Baked Bean Casserole
prep: Preheat your oven to 375°F.
Lightly grease a large casserole dish and set aside.
In a large skillet over medium heat, cook the ground beef until browned.
As it cooks, break the meat into small pieces with a spoon or spatula.
While the beef is cooking, chop the onion and bell pepper into small pieces.
Once the beef is browned, drain the excess fat and add the chopped onion and bell pepper to the skillet.
Cook, stirring occasionally, until the vegetables are soft, about 5 minutes.
Add the pork and beans, barbecue sauce, ketchup, mustard, Worcestershire sauce, soy sauce, and brown sugar to the skillet.
Stir well to combine all the ingredients.
Cut the bacon into small pieces and add them to the mixture.
Stir well to distribute the bacon evenly throughout.
Transfer the mixture from the skillet into the prepared casserole dish.
Spread it out evenly.
Place the casserole in the preheated oven and bake uncovered for about 45 minutes, or until the casserole is bubbly and the bacon is cooked through.
Remove the casserole from the oven and let it sit for about 5 minutes before serving.
This allows the flavors to meld together and the casserole to set slightly, making it easier to serve.
Enjoy your hearty Baked Bean Casserole as a fulfilling main dish or a robust side at your next gathering!

label: Corn Pie
prep: Preheat your oven to 350°F (175°C).
Grease a 9-inch pie dish with a little butter or non-stick cooking spray.
In a small saucepan, melt 2 tablespoons of butter over medium heat.
Stir in 2 tablespoons of flour and ½ teaspoon of salt, whisking continuously to create a smooth roux.
Cook for about 1 minute to remove the raw flour taste.
Gradually add 1¼ cups of milk to the roux, whisking constantly to prevent lumps.
Continue to cook and stir until the mixture thickens and comes to a gentle boil.
Remove from heat.
In a separate bowl, beat 2 eggs.
Temper the eggs by slowly pouring a small amount of the hot milk mixture into the eggs, whisking constantly.
Then, gradually add the tempered eggs back into the saucepan with the remaining milk mixture, whisking continuously.
Stir in 2 cups of fresh corn into the mixture.
Pour the corn mixture into the prepared pie dish.
Sprinkle 1¼ cups of cracker crumbs evenly over the top.
Bake in the preheated oven for 30 to 35 minutes, or until the top is golden brown and the filling is set.
Allow the corn pie to cool for a few minutes before serving.
Enjoy your homemade corn pie warm!

label: Balsamic Chicken & Peppers
prep: Season chicken breasts with salt and pepper on both sides.
Heat 2 tablespoons of olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Add the chicken breasts and cook until golden brown and cooked through, about 5-6 minutes per side.
Remove chicken from the skillet and set aside.
In the same skillet, add the remaining 2 tablespoons of olive oil.
Slice the red and yellow peppers and the onion, then add them to the skillet.
Sauté until the vegetables are soft and slightly caramelized, about 5-7 minutes.
Mince the garlic and add it to the skillet with the peppers and onion.
Cook for an additional 1-2 minutes until fragrant.
Reduce the heat to medium and return the chicken breasts to the skillet.
Drizzle the balsamic vinegar over the chicken and vegetables.
Allow the vinegar to simmer for 2-3 minutes, or until slightly reduced.
Chop the fresh basil and remove the leaves of thyme from their stems.
Sprinkle the herbs over the chicken and vegetables.
Cook for another 2-3 minutes to allow the flavors to meld.
Taste and adjust seasoning with additional salt and pepper if needed.
Serve the balsamic chicken and peppers hot, garnished with additional fresh basil if desired.

label: Smith Island Cake
prep: Preheat your oven to 350°F (175°C).
Grease and flour eight 9-inch round cake pans.
In a medium bowl, whisk together the 14 ounces of all-purpose flour, 2 teaspoons of baking powder, and ½ teaspoon of kosher salt.
Set aside.
In a large bowl, combine the 15.3 ounces of sugar and 2 sticks of melted unsalted butter.
Beat using an electric mixer until well blended.
Add 5 eggs, one at a time, beating well after each addition.
Gradually add the flour mixture to the sugar and butter mixture, alternating with 1 cup of evaporated milk, starting and ending with the flour mixture.
Stir in 2 teaspoons of vanilla extract.
Divide the batter evenly among the prepared pans, using about 1 cup of batter per pan.
Bake in the preheated oven for 15-20 minutes or until a toothpick inserted into the center of each cake layer comes out clean.
Allow the layers to cool in the pans for 10 minutes, then turn out onto wire racks to cool completely.
While the cake layers are cooling, prepare the icing.
In a saucepan over medium heat, combine 2⅔ cups of sugar and 1⅓ cups of evaporated milk.
Bring to a simmer, stirring constantly until the sugar is dissolved.
Add 6 ounces of chopped unsweetened chocolate and 10 tablespoons of melted unsalted butter to the saucepan.
Stir until the chocolate is completely melted and the mixture is smooth.
Remove from heat and stir in 1½ teaspoons of vanilla extract.
Let the icing cool slightly, stirring occasionally to keep it smooth.
To assemble the cake, place one cake layer on a serving plate.
Spread a thin layer of icing over the top.
Repeat with the remaining cake layers, spreading icing between each layer.
Once all the layers are stacked, spread the remaining icing over the top and sides of the cake.
Allow the icing to set before serving.
The Smith Island Cake is best enjoyed at room temperature.

label: Cucumber And Mint Raita
prep: Begin by dry roasting the cumin seeds in a small skillet over medium heat.
Stir constantly for about 1 to 2 minutes, or until the seeds become fragrant and slightly browned.
Remove from heat and allow to cool.
Once cooled, grind the seeds using a mortar and pestle or a spice grinder.
Peel the cucumber and grate it coarsely.
Squeeze the grated cucumber to remove excess water.
In a medium mixing bowl, combine the plain yogurt with the grated cucumber.
Add the freshly chopped mint, ground cumin, salt, cayenne pepper, and a pinch of black pepper to the yogurt mixture.
Stir well to combine all the ingredients thoroughly.
Taste and adjust the seasoning, adding more salt or pepper if needed.
Chill the raita in the refrigerator for at least 30 minutes before serving to allow the flavors to meld together.
Serve the cucumber and mint raita cold as a refreshing side dish or condiment.

label: Carrot Juice
prep: Wash and peel the carrots.
Cut them into manageable pieces that will fit into your juicer.
Wash the apple and cut it into quarters, removing the core.
Roll the lemon on the counter to soften it, then cut it in half.
Juice the carrots, apple, and lemon through a juicer.
Collect the juice in a large container.
Stir the juice well to combine the flavors.
If desired, strain the juice through a fine mesh sieve to remove any pulp for a smoother texture.
Serve the carrot juice immediately over ice, or refrigerate and enjoy chilled.

label: Hello Dolly Bars
prep: Preheat your oven to 350°F (175°C).
Line a 9x13-inch baking pan with parchment paper, allowing some overhang for easy removal.
In a medium bowl, combine 1½ cups cracker crumbs with ½ cup melted butter.
Mix well until the crumbs are evenly moistened.
Press the crumb mixture firmly into the bottom of the prepared baking pan to form a solid, even layer.
Pour 14 ounces of sweetened condensed milk evenly over the crumb layer.
Sprinkle 1 cup of semisweet chocolate chips and 1 cup of butterscotch chips evenly over the condensed milk.
Distribute 1⅓ cups of sweetened coconut over the chocolate and butterscotch chips.
Finally, sprinkle 1 cup of chopped pecans on top.
Bake in the preheated oven for 25 to 30 minutes, or until the edges are golden brown and the middle is set.
Remove from the oven and let cool completely in the pan on a wire rack.
Once cooled, use the overhanging parchment paper to lift the bars out of the pan.
Cut into squares or bars.
Serve and enjoy your Hello Dolly Bars!

label: Quinoa Stuffed Mushrooms
prep: Preheat the oven to 375°F.
Clean the baby portabella mushrooms by gently wiping them with a damp cloth.
Remove the stems, chop them finely, and set aside.
In a small saucepan, bring the chicken stock to a boil.
Add the quinoa, cover, and reduce the heat to low.
Simmer for 15 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed and the quinoa is tender.
While the quinoa is cooking, heat a small skillet over medium heat.
Add a drizzle of olive oil and the chopped mushroom stems.
Sauté for about 3 minutes until they start to soften.
Mince the garlic and add it to the skillet along with the red pepper flakes.
Cook for an additional 1-2 minutes until fragrant.
Chop the parsley finely.
Once the quinoa is cooked, stir in the sautéed mushroom stems, garlic, parsley, and season with salt and pepper to taste.
Mix well.
Arrange the mushroom caps on a baking sheet.
Spoon the quinoa mixture into each mushroom cap, pressing gently to pack it in.
Sprinkle the grated mixed cheese over the stuffed mushrooms.
Bake in the preheated oven for about 20 minutes, or until the mushrooms are tender and the cheese is melted and slightly golden.
Remove from the oven and let cool for a few minutes before serving.
Enjoy your Quinoa Stuffed Mushrooms as a delicious and healthy appetizer or side dish!

label: Garbanzo Bean Soup
prep: Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add the diced tomatoes and fresh rosemary sprigs to the pot.
Cook for about 5 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Drain and rinse the garbanzo beans, then add them to the pot.
Stir to combine.
Pour in enough water to cover the ingredients by about 2 inches.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat and let it simmer for 20 minutes.
Add the pasta to the pot and continue to simmer until the pasta is cooked, about 10-12 minutes, depending on the type of pasta.
Remove the rosemary sprigs.
Taste and adjust seasoning if necessary.
Serve hot, optionally garnished with a drizzle of olive oil or a sprinkle of grated Parmesan cheese.

label: Churro Cheesecake Bars
prep: Preheat your oven to 350°F (175°C).
Grease a 9x13 inch baking pan or line it with parchment paper for easier cleanup.
Unroll one package of crescent rolls and press it into the bottom of the prepared pan, pinching together any seams to form a smooth layer.
In a medium mixing bowl, beat the softened cream cheese until smooth and creamy.
Add ½ cup sugar, the egg, and vanilla extract.
Beat together until well combined and smooth.
Spread the cream cheese mixture evenly over the crescent roll layer in the pan.
Unroll the second package of crescent rolls and carefully place it over the cream cheese layer, pinching together any seams.
In a small bowl, mix together the remaining ½ cup sugar and 2 tablespoons of ground cinnamon.
Sprinkle this cinnamon-sugar mixture evenly over the top crescent roll layer.
Bake in the preheated oven for about 30-35 minutes, or until the crescent dough has puffed up and turned golden brown, and the filling is set.
Remove from the oven and allow to cool completely in the pan on a wire rack.
Once cool, you can cut into bars.
Serve the churro cheesecake bars at room temperature or chilled, depending on your preference.
Enjoy your sweet and creamy treat with a hint of cinnamon spice!

label: Mushroom Quinoa
prep: Rinse the quinoa under cold water until the water runs clear.
In a medium saucepan, bring the chicken stock to a boil.
Add the quinoa to the boiling stock, then reduce the heat to low.
Cover and simmer for 15 minutes, or until the quinoa is tender and the liquid is absorbed.
While the quinoa is cooking, thinly slice the shallots and mushrooms.
Heat the olive oil in a skillet over medium heat.
Add the sliced shallots and mushrooms, sautéing until they are soft and golden, about 5 to 7 minutes.
Once the quinoa is cooked, fluff it with a fork and mix in the sautéed shallots and mushrooms.
Serve warm as a side dish or a light main course.

label: Blueberry Baked Oatmeal
prep: Preheat your oven to 350°F (175°C).
Grease a 9x13 inch baking dish with some of the melted butter or use non-stick spray.
In a large bowl, whisk together the melted butter and ½ cup brown sugar until smooth.
Add the eggs and whisk until fully incorporated.
Stir in the applesauce and milk until everything is well combined.
In another bowl, mix together the quick oats, baking powder, salt, and cinnamon.
Gradually add the dry ingredients to the wet ingredients, stirring until just combined.
Gently fold in the blueberries, being careful not to crush them.
Pour the oatmeal mixture into the prepared baking dish, spreading it out evenly.
Bake in the preheated oven for 35-40 minutes, or until the top is golden brown and the oatmeal is set.
Remove from oven and let cool slightly before serving.
Serve warm, sprinkled with additional brown sugar and a splash of milk if desired.
Enjoy your homemade Blueberry Baked Oatmeal!

label: Leftover Turkey Noodle Soup
prep: Heat the vegetable oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add the chopped carrots, minced garlic, and chopped celery to the pot.
Sauté until the vegetables are softened, about 5 minutes.
Stir in the cooked turkey, dried thyme, salt, and ground black pepper.
Cook for another 2 minutes to blend the flavors.
Pour in the chicken broth and bring the mixture to a boil.
Once boiling, reduce the heat to a simmer and add the egg noodles.
Cook according to the noodle package instructions, usually about 6 to 8 minutes, until the noodles are tender.
Taste and adjust seasoning if necessary.
Serve hot.

label: Honey Lime Chicken Enchiladas
prep: In a small bowl, whisk together honey, lime juice, chili powder, and garlic powder to create the marinade.
Place the chicken in a resealable plastic bag or shallow dish and pour the marinade over the chicken.
Ensure the chicken is well-coated.
Seal or cover, and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, preferably a few hours for better flavor infusion.
Preheat your oven to 350°F (175°C).
Remove the chicken from the marinade and cook in a skillet over medium heat until fully cooked and no longer pink inside, about 7-10 minutes per side.
Once cooked, shred the chicken using two forks.
In a saucepan, combine the enchilada sauce and heavy cream.
Heat over medium heat until it is warm, stirring occasionally.
Dip each tortilla in the warm enchilada sauce mixture briefly to lightly coat.
Fill each tortilla with shredded chicken and a generous amount of shredded jack cheese, reserving some cheese for topping.
Roll up the tortillas and place them seam side down in a greased 9x13 inch baking dish.
Pour the remaining enchilada sauce and cream mixture over the rolled enchiladas.
Sprinkle the remaining shredded cheese over the top.
Bake in the preheated oven for 20-25 minutes, or until the cheese is bubbly and lightly browned.
Remove from oven and let sit for a few minutes before serving.
Enjoy your Honey Lime Chicken Enchiladas hot.

label: Crunchy Asian Salad
prep: In a large mixing bowl, combine the shredded cabbage, sliced scallions, shredded carrots, and diced chicken.
In a small skillet over medium heat, toast the slivered almonds and sesame seeds, stirring frequently, until golden brown and fragrant, about 3-5 minutes.
Remove from heat and let cool.
In a separate small bowl, whisk together the vegetable oil, white vinegar, low-sodium soy sauce, ground black pepper, sugar, and the contents of the seasoning package to create the dressing.
Pour the dressing over the cabbage mixture in the large bowl.
Toss well to ensure all ingredients are evenly coated with the dressing.
Sprinkle the toasted almonds and sesame seeds over the salad.
Toss lightly to distribute them throughout the salad.
Chill the salad in the refrigerator for at least 30 minutes to allow the flavors to meld.
Serve the Crunchy Asian Salad chilled, perfect as a refreshing side dish or a light main course.

label: Chicken Pot Pie With Biscuit Topping
prep: Preheat your oven to 375°F (190°C).
In a large skillet, melt 2 teaspoons of butter over medium heat.
Add the diced onions and sauté until they become translucent, about 5 minutes.
Add the diced potatoes and carrots to the skillet.
Cook, stirring occasionally, for about 10 minutes, or until the vegetables start to soften.
Sprinkle 2 teaspoons of flour over the vegetables and stir to coat.
Cook for an additional 2 minutes to remove the raw flour taste.
Add the diced chicken to the skillet and stir to combine.
Pour in the chicken stock and ⅓ cup of whole milk.
Bring the mixture to a simmer, and let it cook until the sauce thickens and the vegetables are tender, about 10 minutes.
Stir in the frozen peas and 1 teaspoon of sea salt.
Cook for another 5 minutes, then remove from heat.
To make the biscuit topping, in a large bowl, combine 1¾ cups of flour, ½ teaspoon of sea salt, and 1 teaspoon of baking powder.
Cut in 7 teaspoons of softened butter using a pastry cutter or two knives until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs.
Gradually add ¾ cups of milk to the flour mixture, stirring until the dough just comes together.
Turn the dough out onto a lightly floured surface and knead gently just until it forms a soft ball.
Roll the dough out to about ½ inch thickness.
Cut into rounds using a biscuit cutter or the rim of a glass.
Pour the chicken and vegetable mixture into a 9-inch pie dish or an equivalent-sized baking dish.
Arrange the biscuit rounds on top of the filling, covering it completely.
Bake in the preheated oven for 20-25 minutes, or until the biscuits are golden brown and the filling is bubbly.
Let the chicken pot pie stand for 5 minutes before serving.
