Enjoy your homemade Chicken Pot Pie with Biscuit Topping!

label: Sticky Sesame Chicken
prep: Preheat your oven to 375°F.
Line a baking sheet with aluminum foil and lightly grease it with cooking spray or a bit of oil.
In a small bowl, whisk together the honey, soy sauce, and fresh lemon juice until well combined.
Place the sesame seeds in a shallow dish.
Cut the chicken thighs into bite-sized pieces.
Dip each piece first into the honey soy mixture, then roll them in the sesame seeds until well coated.
Arrange the coated chicken pieces on the prepared baking sheet, making sure they are not touching each other.
Bake in the preheated oven for about 25 to 30 minutes, or until the chicken is fully cooked through and the sesame seeds are nicely toasted.
Remove from the oven and let the chicken rest for a few minutes before serving.
This allows the juices to redistribute and the coating to set slightly.
Serve the sticky sesame chicken hot, garnished with additional sesame seeds or a sprinkle of chopped green onions if desired.
Enjoy your delicious and easy-to-make dish!

label: Steak With Peppercorn Sauce
prep: Pat the steak dry with paper towels and season generously with salt.
Let it sit at room temperature for about 15 minutes.
Heat a skillet over medium-high heat and add the olive oil.
Once hot, add the steak to the skillet.
Cook the steak for about 4-5 minutes on each side for medium-rare, or longer depending on your desired doneness.
Once cooked, transfer the steak to a plate and cover loosely with foil to keep warm.
In the same skillet, reduce the heat to medium.
Add the green peppercorns and sauté for about 1 minute.
Mix the cornstarch and brown sugar with the beef broth in a small bowl until well combined.
Pour this mixture into the skillet with the peppercorns.
Bring the sauce to a simmer, stirring constantly, until it starts to thicken, about 3-4 minutes.
Reduce the heat to low and stir in the cream cheese until the sauce is smooth and creamy.
Taste the sauce and adjust seasoning with salt if needed.
Slice the steak against the grain and serve it with the peppercorn sauce drizzled over the top.

label: Chocolate Raspberry Cheesecake
prep: Preheat your oven to 350°F (175°C).
Lightly grease a 9-inch springform pan.
Crush the chocolate cookies into fine crumbs using a food processor or a rolling pin.
Mix the cookie crumbs with the melted butter until well combined.
Press this mixture into the bottom of the prepared springform pan to form the crust.
Place in the refrigerator to chill while you prepare the filling.
In a large mixing bowl, beat the cream cheese until smooth using an electric mixer.
Gradually add the granulated sugar and cornstarch, beating until creamy and smooth.
Mix in the vanilla extract.
Add the eggs one at a time, beating well after each addition.
Mix in the sour cream until the mixture is smooth.
Melt the dark chocolate in a microwave-safe bowl or using a double boiler, stirring until smooth.
Allow the chocolate to cool slightly, then fold it into the cream cheese mixture until well combined.
Pour half of the cream cheese mixture over the chilled crust.
Spoon half of the thawed raspberries over the filling.
Pour the remaining cream cheese mixture over the raspberries, smoothing the top with a spatula.
Bake in the preheated oven for 45-55 minutes, or until the edges are set and the center is slightly jiggly.
Turn off the oven, slightly open the oven door, and allow the cheesecake to cool in the oven for 1 hour to prevent cracking.
Remove the cheesecake from the oven and let it cool completely at room temperature.
Once cooled, refrigerate for at least 4 hours, preferably overnight.
Before serving, top the cheesecake with the remaining raspberries.
Optionally, you can drizzle with melted chocolate or dust with powdered sugar for extra decoration.
To serve, carefully remove the sides of the springform pan, slice, and enjoy your Chocolate Raspberry Cheesecake.

label: Potstickers
prep: In a large mixing bowl, combine the ground pork, shredded Napa cabbage, shredded carrot, minced green onions, minced garlic, minced ginger, soy sauce, toasted sesame oil, egg, kosher salt, and black pepper.
Mix thoroughly until all ingredients are well incorporated.
Lay a potsticker wrapper flat on a clean surface.
Place about 1 tablespoon of the pork mixture in the center of the wrapper.
Moisten the edges of the wrapper with water using your finger.
Fold the wrapper over the filling to form a half-moon shape.
Pinch the edges together to seal, making sure to remove any air pockets.
Optionally, create pleats along the edge for a traditional look.
Repeat with the remaining wrappers and filling.
Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Once hot, arrange the potstickers in a single layer in the skillet and fry for about 2 to 3 minutes, or until the bottoms are golden brown.
Carefully add 1/2 cup of water to the skillet (the oil may splatter, so be cautious), and immediately cover with a lid.
Let the potstickers steam for about 5 to 7 minutes, or until the water has evaporated and the wrappers are tender.
Remove the lid and allow the potstickers to cook for an additional 1 to 2 minutes to crisp up the bottoms again.
Serve hot with a dipping sauce made from equal parts soy sauce and vinegar, and a dash of chili oil or sesame oil, if desired.
Enjoy your homemade potstickers!

label: Coconut Hot Chocolate
prep: In a medium saucepan, combine the coconut milk and chocolate.
Heat over medium heat, stirring constantly, until the chocolate is completely melted and the mixture is smooth.
Stir in the vanilla extract and continue to heat, stirring occasionally, until the mixture is hot but not boiling.
Remove the saucepan from the heat.
Divide the hot chocolate mixture among four mugs.
Add a scoop of chocolate ice cream to each mug.
Top each mug with whipped cream and sprinkle with your choice of fruit.
Serve immediately and enjoy your creamy Coconut Hot Chocolate.

label: Cod Stew
prep: Begin by preparing the vegetables.
Peel and chop the onions, dice the tomatoes, and slice the red and green peppers into strips.
Peel and cut the potatoes into bite-sized chunks.
Mince the garlic cloves.
In a large pot, heat the olive oil over medium heat.
Add the chopped onions and minced garlic, sautéing until the onions become translucent, about 5 minutes.
Add the diced tomatoes and pepper strips to the pot.
Cook for another 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the tomatoes start to break down and the peppers soften.
Stir in the potatoes, and add enough water to just cover the ingredients.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Add the bay leaf.
Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat to a simmer.
Allow the stew to simmer for about 20 minutes, or until the potatoes are nearly tender.
While the stew simmers, prepare the cod steaks by cutting them into large chunks, ensuring any bones are removed.
Add the cod chunks to the pot, gently placing them on top of the simmering vegetables.
Cover the pot and let it simmer for an additional 10-15 minutes, or until the cod is cooked through and flakes easily with a fork.
Remove the bay leaf and adjust seasoning with additional salt and pepper if needed.
Serve the cod stew hot, ideally with crusty bread or over a bed of rice to soak up the flavorful broth.
Enjoy your hearty and delicious meal!

label: Champ
prep: Peel and quarter the potatoes.
Place them in a large pot and cover with cold water.
Add 1 teaspoon of salt.
Bring the water to a boil over high heat, then reduce to a simmer and cook the potatoes until they are tender, about 15 to 20 minutes.
While the potatoes are cooking, finely chop the shallots.
In a small saucepan, melt the butter over medium heat.
Add the chopped shallots and sauté until they are soft and translucent, about 5 to 7 minutes.
Add the milk to the shallots and butter, and warm gently.
Do not boil.
Keep warm until the potatoes are cooked.
Once the potatoes are tender, drain them well and return them to the pot.
Mash the potatoes until smooth.
Gradually add the warm milk, shallots, and butter mixture to the mashed potatoes, mixing until well combined and creamy.
Adjust seasoning with additional salt, if needed.
Serve the champ hot, ideally as a side dish with meats or vegetables.

label: Slow Cooker Sweet Potato Soup
prep: Peel and chop the sweet potatoes into cubes.
Peel and slice the carrot.
Peel and finely chop the red onion and ginger.
Place the sweet potatoes, carrot, red onion, and ginger into a slow cooker.
Add 1½ cups of vegetable broth to the slow cooker.
Stir in the cayenne pepper, cumin, turmeric, and nutmeg.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Cover and cook on low for 6-8 hours, or on high for 3-4 hours, until the sweet potatoes and carrots are tender.
Once the vegetables are cooked, use an immersion blender to puree the soup directly in the slow cooker until smooth.
Alternatively, you can transfer the mixture to a blender and puree it in batches, then return it to the slow cooker.
Stir in ½ cup of lite coconut milk and continue to heat the soup for another 10-15 minutes until it is heated through.
Taste and adjust the seasoning if necessary.
If the soup is too thick, you can add a little more vegetable broth or coconut milk to reach your desired consistency.
Serve the soup hot, drizzled with the remaining 2 tablespoons of lite coconut milk.
Optionally, garnish with a sprinkle of chopped herbs like cilantro or parsley for added color and flavor.

label: Sesame Chicken With Broccoli
prep: In a large bowl, combine 6 tablespoons of cornstarch, 1 teaspoon of kosher salt, and ½ teaspoon of ground black pepper.
Mix well.
Cut the chicken breasts into bite-sized pieces and add them to the cornstarch mixture.
Toss until the chicken is fully coated.
Heat 4 tablespoons of vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Once hot, add the chicken pieces in batches, making sure not to overcrowd the pan.
Cook until golden and crispy, about 3-4 minutes per side.
Remove the chicken and set aside on a paper towel-lined plate.
In the same skillet, add the broccoli florets and stir-fry for about 4-5 minutes or until they are bright green and slightly tender.
Remove the broccoli from the skillet and set aside.
In a small bowl, whisk together 5 tablespoons of honey, 4 tablespoons of low-sodium soy sauce, 3 tablespoons of rice wine vinegar, 1 tablespoon of sriracha, grated garlic, and grated ginger.
Pour the sauce mixture into the skillet and bring to a simmer.
Let it cook for about 2 minutes or until slightly thickened.
Return the chicken and broccoli to the skillet.
Toss everything together to coat with the sauce.
Cook for an additional 2-3 minutes, ensuring everything is heated through and well combined.
Drizzle 1½ teaspoons of toasted sesame oil over the chicken and broccoli.
Sprinkle with 2 tablespoons of sesame seeds.
Slice the scallions and scatter them over the top as a garnish.
Serve the sesame chicken with broccoli hot, ideally over a bed of steamed rice.
Enjoy your flavorful and hearty meal!

label: Sufganiyot
prep: In a small saucepan, gently heat the milk until it is warm but not hot (about 110°F).
Remove from heat.
In a large mixing bowl, combine the warm milk, yeast, and 1 tablespoon of the granulated sugar.
Stir lightly and let sit until the mixture is frothy, about 5 to 10 minutes.
Add the remaining sugar, egg yolks, and salt to the yeast mixture.
Mix well until all ingredients are incorporated.
Gradually add the flour to the wet ingredients, mixing continuously until a soft dough forms.
Add the unsalted butter to the dough, and knead it into the dough until fully incorporated.
Continue to knead the dough on a lightly floured surface for about 8 to 10 minutes, or until it is smooth and elastic.
Place the kneaded dough in a lightly oiled bowl, cover with a clean cloth, and let it rise in a warm place until it has doubled in size, about 1 to 1.5 hours.
Once the dough has risen, punch it down gently and turn it out onto a lightly floured surface.
Roll the dough out to about ½ inch thickness.
Using a round cutter or a glass, cut out circles from the dough.
Place the dough circles on a parchment-lined baking sheet, cover them with a cloth, and let them rise again until puffy, about 30 minutes.
Heat the canola oil in a deep fryer or large heavy pot to 350°F.
Carefully place a few dough circles into the hot oil.
Fry the sufganiyot until golden brown on both sides, about 1 to 2 minutes per side.
Use a slotted spoon to remove them from the oil and set them on a paper towel-lined plate to drain.
Once all the sufganiyot are fried and slightly cooled, fill a piping bag with the jam.
Insert the tip of the piping bag into the side of each sufganiyot and gently fill with jam.
Dust the filled sufganiyot with powdered sugar before serving.
Enjoy your homemade sufganiyot!

label: Yeast Bread
prep: In a small bowl, dissolve the yeast in ½ cup warm water (about 110°F).
Let it sit for 5 minutes until it becomes frothy, indicating that the yeast is active.
In a saucepan, heat the milk until it is warm but not boiling.
Add the sugar, salt, and shortening, stirring until the shortening is melted and the sugar and salt are dissolved.
Remove from heat and let cool to lukewarm.
In a large mixing bowl, combine the yeast mixture with the lukewarm milk mixture.
Gradually add about 6 cups of flour, one cup at a time, stirring with a wooden spoon until the dough begins to come together.
Continue adding flour, one cup at a time, until the dough becomes too stiff to stir with a spoon.
Turn the dough out onto a floured surface and knead, incorporating more flour as needed, until the dough is smooth and elastic, about 8 to 10 minutes.
Place the kneaded dough in a large greased bowl, turning it to grease all sides.
Cover the bowl with a clean cloth and let the dough rise in a warm, draft-free place until it has doubled in size, about 1 to 1½ hours.
Punch down the risen dough and turn it out onto a floured surface.
Divide the dough into two equal parts.
Shape each part into a loaf and place each loaf into a greased 9x5-inch loaf pan.
Cover the loaf pans with a clean cloth and let the dough rise again until it has doubled in size, about 45 minutes to 1 hour.
Preheat the oven to 375°F.
Once the dough has risen, uncover the loaves and place them in the oven.
Bake for about 30 to 35 minutes, or until the loaves are golden brown and sound hollow when tapped.
Remove the bread from the oven and turn out the loaves onto a wire rack to cool completely before slicing.
Enjoy your homemade yeast bread, perfect for sandwiches, toast, or simply buttered as a delicious snack.

label: Microwave Rice
prep: In a microwave-safe bowl, combine 2 cups of water, 1 cup of long grain rice, and ½ teaspoon of salt.
Stir the mixture to ensure the salt is evenly distributed.
Cover the bowl with a microwave-safe lid or a microwave-safe plastic wrap.
Make sure to leave a small vent for steam to escape.
Microwave on high for 5 minutes.
After the initial 5 minutes, reduce the power to medium (50% power) and microwave for an additional 15 minutes.
Carefully remove the bowl from the microwave (the bowl will be hot, so use oven mitts).
Let it sit covered for 5 minutes to allow the rice to finish absorbing any remaining water.
Fluff the rice with a fork to separate the grains before serving.

label: Cheese Nachos
prep: In a medium saucepan, melt the butter over medium heat.
Add the diced onion, minced garlic, and jalapeño to the saucepan.
Sauté until the onions are translucent and the garlic is fragrant, about 3-5 minutes.
Stir in the flour and cook for about 1 minute, stirring constantly to prevent burning.
This will create a roux, which will help thicken the cheese sauce.
Gradually add the milk to the saucepan, whisking continuously to ensure the mixture stays smooth and free of lumps.
Bring the mixture to a simmer and continue to cook until it thickens slightly, about 5-7 minutes.
Reduce the heat to low and gradually add the grated cheddar cheese, stirring until the cheese is completely melted and the sauce is smooth.
Serve the warm cheese sauce over your favorite nachos and enjoy!

label: Fabulous Frittata
prep: Preheat your oven to 375°F.
Lightly grease a 9-inch pie dish or ovenproof skillet with 1 tablespoon of olive oil.
Wash and thinly slice the red potatoes.
In a skillet over medium heat, heat 1 tablespoon of olive oil.
Add the sliced potatoes and cook until they are golden and tender, about 8-10 minutes.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
While the potatoes are cooking, whisk the eggs in a large bowl until well beaten.
Stir in the cottage cheese, chopped chives, and additional salt and pepper to taste.
Once the potatoes are cooked, add the baby spinach to the skillet and cook until just wilted, about 1-2 minutes.
Slice the roasted red bell pepper into thin strips and add them to the skillet with the potatoes and spinach, stirring to combine.
Pour the egg and cottage cheese mixture over the vegetables in the skillet, gently stirring to ensure the ingredients are evenly distributed.
Transfer the skillet to the preheated oven and bake the frittata for 25-30 minutes, or until the eggs are set and the top is lightly golden.
Remove the frittata from the oven and let it cool for a few minutes before slicing.
Serve warm, garnished with additional chives if desired.

label: Plum Sorbet
prep: Wash the plums thoroughly, then cut them in half to remove the pits.
Place the pitted plum halves into a blender or food processor.
Squeeze the juice from the half lemon into the blender.
Add the ½ cup of sugar syrup to the blender.
Blend the mixture until it is smooth and the plums are fully pureed.
Taste the mixture and adjust the sweetness or tartness, if necessary, by adding a little more sugar syrup or lemon juice.
Pour the plum mixture into a shallow baking dish or a sorbet machine, if you have one.
If using a baking dish, place it in the freezer.
Stir the mixture every 30 minutes with a fork to break up ice crystals, until it is evenly frozen.
This process may take about 2 to 3 hours.
Once the sorbet is frozen, scoop it into serving dishes.
Serve immediately or store in the freezer in an airtight container until ready to serve.

label: Irish Soda Bread Muffins
prep: Preheat your oven to 400°F (200°C).
Grease a 12-cup muffin tin or line with muffin papers.
In a large mixing bowl, whisk together the all-purpose flour, ½ cup plus 2 tablespoons white sugar, baking powder, salt, and baking soda.
Stir in the caraway seeds and raisins to coat them with flour.
In a separate bowl, beat the egg lightly.
Stir in the buttermilk and melted butter.
Make a well in the center of the dry ingredients and pour in the buttermilk mixture.
Stir just until the dry ingredients are moistened; do not overmix.
Spoon the batter into the prepared muffin cups, filling each about three-quarters full.
Bake in the preheated oven for 15-20 minutes, or until the tops are golden and a toothpick inserted into the center of a muffin comes out clean.
Remove the muffins from the oven and let them cool in the pan for a few minutes, then transfer to a wire rack to cool completely.
Serve warm or at room temperature.
Enjoy your Irish Soda Bread Muffins with a spread of butter or jam if desired.

label: Garden Fresh Tomato Soup
prep: In a large pot, melt the butter and 2 tablespoons of olive oil over medium heat.
Add the chopped onion, thyme sprigs, and basil leaves.
Cook, stirring occasionally, until the onion is translucent, about 5-7 minutes.
Stir in the diced tomatoes, tomato paste, salt, and black pepper.
Cook for 10 minutes, allowing the tomatoes to soften and release their juices.
Sprinkle the flour over the tomato mixture and stir well to combine.
Cook for 2 minutes to remove the raw flour taste.
Gradually add 3 cups of chicken broth, stirring constantly to prevent lumps.
Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat and simmer for 20 minutes.
Remove from heat and discard the thyme sprigs and basil leaves.
Use an immersion blender to puree the soup directly in the pot until smooth.
Alternatively, you can transfer the mixture to a blender and puree in batches, then return to the pot.
Stir in the sugar and heavy whipping cream.
Heat the soup over low heat, just until hot.
Do not boil after adding the cream.
In a separate pan, heat 2 tablespoons of olive oil over medium heat.
Add the sliced garlic and cook until fragrant, about 1 minute.
Brush the Italian bread slices with the garlic-infused olive oil and toast in the pan until golden brown on both sides.
Serve the soup hot, garnished with a drizzle of olive oil and a slice of toasted garlic bread on the side.

label: Salmon Wellington
prep: Preheat your oven to 400°F.
Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
In a large skillet, melt 2 tablespoons of unsalted butter over medium heat.
Add the chopped mushrooms and minced shallots, cooking until the mushrooms are soft and browned, about 8-10 minutes.
Season the mushroom mixture with ½ teaspoon fine sea salt, ¼ teaspoon black pepper, and 1 teaspoon chopped fresh thyme.
Stir well to combine.
Add the chopped spinach to the skillet, cooking until the spinach is wilted and any excess moisture has evaporated, about 2-3 minutes.
Remove from heat and let the mixture cool slightly.
On a lightly floured surface, roll out the puff pastry into a rectangle large enough to encase the salmon fillets.
If necessary, join two pieces by overlapping slightly and pressing the edges together.
Place the salmon fillets on the puff pastry, spacing them evenly.
Season the salmon with the remaining ½ teaspoon salt and ¼ teaspoon black pepper.
Divide the mushroom and spinach mixture evenly over the top of each salmon fillet.
Fold the puff pastry over the salmon and filling, trimming any excess pastry.
Press the edges to seal, and crimp with a fork for a decorative touch.
In a small bowl, beat the egg with 1 tablespoon of water to make an egg wash.
Brush the egg wash over the puff pastry.
Transfer the prepared Wellingtons to the prepared baking sheet.
Bake in the preheated oven for 20-25 minutes, or until the pastry is golden brown and puffed.
While the Wellingtons bake, prepare the red wine sauce.
In a small saucepan, melt the remaining 1½ tablespoons of butter over medium heat.
Add the remaining 1 teaspoon of chopped thyme and cook for 1 minute.
Pour in the red wine, bring to a simmer, and reduce by half, about 10-12 minutes, until the sauce thickens slightly.
Remove the Wellingtons from the oven and let them rest for a few minutes before serving.
Serve each Wellington sliced, with the red wine sauce drizzled over the top.
ingredientLines: ½ teaspoon black pepper, divided, ground

label: Roast Beef With Gravy
prep: Preheat your oven to 375°F.
Rub the beef roast with 1 tablespoon of olive oil, 1 teaspoon of Aromatic Bitters, and a generous amount of salt, ensuring it's evenly coated.
In a roasting pan, heat the remaining 1 tablespoon of olive oil over medium heat.
Add the half onion (chopped) and garlic cloves (minced) to the pan and sauté until they start to soften and become fragrant, about 2-3 minutes.
Place the seasoned beef roast in the roasting pan.
Sear each side of the roast for about 3-4 minutes until it develops a nice brown crust.
Pour ½ cup of water and the can of beef broth into the pan around the roast.
Drizzle the remaining 1 teaspoon of Aromatic Bitters over the roast.
Transfer the roasting pan to the preheated oven and roast for about 60-75 minutes, or until a meat thermometer inserted into the thickest part of the roast reads 135°F for medium-rare.
Once the roast is cooked to your liking, remove it from the oven and place it on a cutting board.
Tent it loosely with foil and let it rest for about 15-20 minutes.
While the roast is resting, prepare the gravy.
Place the roasting pan over two burners on medium heat.
Sprinkle the flour over the juices in the pan, and whisk continuously to combine.
Cook for 2-3 minutes until the flour is lightly browned.
Gradually whisk in the brandy, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan.
Allow the gravy to simmer and thicken for about 5 minutes, adjusting the seasoning with salt as needed.
Slice the roast beef thinly against the grain.
Serve the slices with the warm gravy poured over the top.

label: Pinwheels
prep: Soften the cream cheese to room temperature to ensure it spreads easily.
Lay out the flour tortillas on a clean, flat surface.
Spread each tortilla evenly with the softened cream cheese, covering the entire surface to the edges.
Distribute the turkey slices evenly over the cream cheese on each tortilla.
Sprinkle the chopped green onions over the turkey layers on each tortilla.
Carefully roll up each tortilla tightly to ensure the fillings are secured inside.
Once all tortillas are rolled, use a sharp knife to slice each roll into 1-inch thick pinwheels.
Arrange the pinwheels on a serving platter, standing them on their sides so the spiral pattern is visible.
Serve immediately or cover and refrigerate until ready to serve, allowing the flavors to meld together nicely.

label: Bacon And Egg Potato Salad
prep: Place potatoes in a large pot and cover with cold water.
Bring to a boil over high heat, then reduce to a simmer.
Cook until potatoes are tender, about 15-20 minutes.
Drain and let cool slightly, then cut into bite-sized pieces.
While the potatoes are cooking, place eggs in a saucepan and cover with cold water.
Bring to a boil, then cover and remove from heat.
Let stand for 12 minutes.
Drain, cool in ice water, peel, and chop.
In a large skillet, cook the chopped bacon over medium heat until crisp.
Remove bacon with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels.
In a large bowl, whisk together mayonnaise, mustard, red wine vinegar, sugar, salt, and pepper to taste.
Chop the scallions and red onion, and add to the bowl with the dressing.
Add the minced parsley.
Add the chopped potatoes, eggs, and cooked bacon to the bowl.
Gently fold everything together until well coated with the dressing.
Taste and adjust seasoning with additional salt and pepper if needed.
Refrigerate the potato salad for at least an hour before serving to allow flavors to meld.
Serve chilled or at room temperature.

label: Maple Pecan Scones
prep: Preheat your oven to 400°F (200°C).
Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
In a large bowl, whisk together 2¾ cups flour, ⅓ cup brown sugar, ½ teaspoon salt, and 1 tablespoon baking powder.
Cut ½ cup of cold butter into small pieces and add to the flour mixture.
Use a pastry cutter or your fingers to blend the butter into the flour until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs.
Stir in 1 cup of chopped pecans.
In a separate bowl, whisk together 2 eggs, 2 teaspoons vanilla extract, and ½ cup heavy cream.
Gradually add the wet ingredients to the dry ingredients, stirring until just combined.
Be careful not to overmix.
Turn the dough out onto a lightly floured surface and knead gently a few times.
Pat the dough into a round shape about 1 inch thick.
Cut the dough into 8 wedges and place them on the prepared baking sheet, spacing them about 2 inches apart.
Bake in the preheated oven for 15-20 minutes, or until golden brown and cooked through.
While the scones are baking, prepare the maple glaze.
In a small bowl, whisk together 2 cups powdered sugar, ¼ cup maple syrup, and 2½ tablespoons milk until smooth.
Remove the scones from the oven and let them cool on the baking sheet for about 10 minutes, then transfer to a wire rack.
Drizzle the maple glaze over the warm scones.
Allow the glaze to set before serving.
Enjoy your Maple Pecan Scones!

label: Cake Mix Cinnamon Rolls
prep: In a large bowl, combine 2 cups of flour, yellow cake mix, and yeast.
Stir well to blend.
Heat water to 120°F to 130°F and add it to the flour mixture.
Stir until well combined, then gradually add enough of the remaining flour to make a soft dough.
Turn the dough out onto a floured surface and knead until smooth and elastic, about 5 minutes.
Place the dough in a greased bowl, turning once to grease the top.
Cover and let rise in a warm place until doubled in size, about 1 hour.
Punch down the dough and turn it out onto a floured surface.
Roll the dough into a large rectangle, about 1/2 inch thick.
Melt ¼ cup of butter and brush it over the surface of the dough.
In a small bowl, mix together the sugar and cinnamon, then sprinkle evenly over the buttered dough.
Starting with one long side, roll up the dough tightly.
Pinch the seam to seal.
Cut the roll into 12 equal slices.
Place the slices, cut side down, in a greased 13x9 inch baking pan.
Cover and let rise until nearly doubled, about 30 minutes.
Preheat the oven to 375°F.
Bake the cinnamon rolls for 20 to 25 minutes, or until golden brown.
While the rolls are baking, prepare the frosting.
In a medium bowl, beat together 6 tablespoons of butter, confectioners' sugar, vanilla, and milk until smooth and spreadable.
Remove the rolls from the oven and allow to cool slightly.
Spread the frosting over the warm rolls before serving.

label: Pepperoni Lasagna
prep: Preheat your oven to 375°F (190°C).
Begin by cooking the lasagna noodles according to the package instructions until al dente.
Drain and set aside.
In a large skillet, brown the ground beef over medium heat.
Finely chop the onion and add it to the skillet.
Cook until the meat is thoroughly browned and the onion is tender.
Add the tomato sauce, tomato paste, water, beef bouillon granules, dried parsley, Italian seasoning, 1 teaspoon salt, and garlic salt to the skillet.
Stir well to combine.
Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat and simmer, uncovered, for about 30 minutes, stirring occasionally.
In a medium bowl, beat the eggs.
Mix in the cottage cheese and sour cream until well combined.
To assemble the lasagna, spread a thin layer of the meat sauce in the bottom of a 9x13 inch baking dish.
Place a layer of cooked lasagna noodles over the sauce.
Spread half of the cottage cheese mixture over the noodles.
Layer half of the sliced pepperoni over the cottage cheese mixture, then sprinkle with 1 cup of mozzarella cheese.
Repeat the layers, starting with the meat sauce, then noodles, the remaining cottage cheese mixture, the remaining pepperoni, and another cup of mozzarella cheese.
Top the final layer with the remaining meat sauce.
Sprinkle the grated Parmesan cheese evenly over the top.
Cover the baking dish with aluminum foil and bake in the preheated oven for 25 minutes.
After 25 minutes, remove the foil and continue baking for an additional 25 minutes, or until the cheese is bubbly and golden brown.
Remove from the oven and let the lasagna stand for about 10 minutes before slicing and serving.
This allows the layers to set and makes it easier to cut.
Enjoy your homemade Pepperoni Lasagna!

label: Grilled Chicken Skewers
prep: Cut the chicken breast meat into 1-inch cubes and place them in a large bowl.
Season the chicken cubes generously with salt and black pepper.
Pour ½ cup of balsamic vinaigrette over the seasoned chicken, ensuring all pieces are well coated.
Cover the bowl and marinate in the refrigerator for at least 1 hour, or up to 4 hours for deeper flavor.
Preheat the grill to medium-high heat.
If using wooden skewers, soak them in water for at least 30 minutes to prevent burning.
Thread the marinated chicken cubes alternately with the cut vegetables onto the skewers.
Oil the grill grates lightly to prevent sticking.
Place the skewers on the grill.
Grill the skewers, turning occasionally, until the chicken is thoroughly cooked and the vegetables are tender and slightly charred, about 10 to 15 minutes.
Remove the skewers from the grill and let them rest for a few minutes.
Sprinkle the grilled chicken skewers with chopped fresh parsley before serving.

label: Slow Cooker Chicken Carnitas
prep: Place the chicken breasts in the bottom of a slow cooker.
Chop the ½ onion finely and add it to the slow cooker.

In a small bowl, mix together the chicken broth, juice of 2 limes, ¼ cup orange juice, 1½ teaspoons chili powder, 1 teaspoon cumin, 1 teaspoon garlic powder, 1 teaspoon oregano, 2 bay leaves, 1 teaspoon salt, and 1 teaspoon pepper.
Pour the mixture over the chicken in the slow cooker, ensuring the chicken is well-coated with the spices and liquids.
Cover and cook on low for 6-7 hours or on high for 3-4 hours, until the chicken is tender and easily shreds with a fork.
Once cooked, remove the chicken from the slow cooker and shred it using two forks.
If desired, preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
Add the shredded chicken and some of the cooking liquid from the slow cooker.
Sauté until the chicken is crispy and browned on the edges.
Serve the chicken carnitas in tacos, burritos, or over rice, garnished with fresh lime wedges, chopped cilantro, or your favorite toppings.

label: Eggnog Muffins
prep: Preheat your oven to 375°F (190°C).
Grease or line a 12-cup muffin tin with paper liners.
In a large mixing bowl, cream together ¼ cup butter and ¾ cups sugar until light and fluffy.
Beat in the 2 eggs one at a time, then stir in 1 teaspoon vanilla extract.
In a separate bowl, whisk together 2½ cups all-purpose flour, 2 teaspoons baking powder, 1½ teaspoons ground nutmeg, and ½ teaspoon salt.
Gradually add the dry ingredients to the creamed mixture alternately with 1½ cups eggnog, starting and ending with the flour mixture.
Stir just until combined.
Spoon the batter into the prepared muffin cups, filling each about two-thirds full.
To make the topping, in a small bowl, combine ½ cup sugar, ½ cup all-purpose flour, ¾ teaspoons nutmeg, and ¼ teaspoon eggnog.
Mix in 3 tablespoons melted butter until the mixture is crumbly.
Sprinkle the topping evenly over the batter in the muffin cups.
Bake in the preheated oven for 20-25 minutes, or until a toothpick inserted into the center of a muffin comes out clean.
Allow the muffins to cool in the pan for 5 minutes before transferring them to a wire rack to cool completely.
Enjoy your Eggnog Muffins warm or at room temperature for a festive treat!

label: Instant Pot Spanish Rice
prep: Set your Instant Pot to the sauté setting and heat the olive oil.
Add the finely chopped onion and minced garlic to the pot.
Sauté until the onions become translucent, about 2-3 minutes.
Stir in the rice and cook for another minute, ensuring the rice is well coated with the oil and lightly toasted.
Pour in the chicken broth and water, then add the chili powder, cayenne pepper, and salt.
Stir well to combine all the ingredients.
Add the can of diced tomatoes, including the juice, to the pot.
Do not stir after adding the tomatoes; this helps prevent the burn signal.
Secure the lid of the Instant Pot and set the valve to the sealing position.
Select the manual or pressure cook setting and set the time for 7 minutes at high pressure.
Once the cooking time has finished, allow the pressure to release naturally for 10 minutes, then carefully turn the valve to venting to release any remaining pressure.
Open the lid, fluff the rice with a fork, and mix everything gently to distribute the tomatoes evenly.
Serve the Spanish rice hot as a side dish or as part of a main meal.
Enjoy!

label: Zeppole
prep: In a large mixing bowl, combine the ricotta cheese and eggs.
Mix well until smooth.
Add the flour, baking soda, salt, 3 tablespoons granulated sugar, and vanilla extract to the ricotta mixture.
Stir until just combined; the batter should be thick and creamy.
In a small shallow bowl, mix together ½ cup sugar and 1 tablespoon cinnamon.
Set aside for coating the cooked zeppole.
Heat the vegetable oil in a deep fryer or large heavy-bottomed pot to 375°F.
Use a candy thermometer to monitor the temperature.
Carefully drop tablespoons of the batter into the hot oil, working in batches to avoid overcrowding.
Fry the zeppole until they are golden brown and puffed, about 3 to 4 minutes, turning them occasionally for even cooking.
Using a slotted spoon, remove the zeppole from the oil and drain on paper towels briefly.
While still warm, roll the zeppole in the cinnamon-sugar mixture until well coated.
Serve warm for the best flavor and texture.
Enjoy your homemade zeppole!

label: Salmon Bisque
prep: Prepare the vegetables: Finely chop the carrots, shallots, celery, and garlic.
Slice the shiitake mushrooms.
In a large pot, melt the butter over medium heat.
Add the chopped shallots, celery, carrots, and garlic.
Sauté until the vegetables are softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Stir in the flour, thyme, paprika, and celery salt.
Cook for 2 minutes to remove the raw flour taste, stirring constantly.
Gradually add the chicken broth to the pot, stirring continuously to prevent lumps.
Add the bay leaves.
Bring the mixture to a simmer.
Add the sliced shiitake mushrooms to the pot.
Simmer for 10 minutes.
While the vegetables are simmering, season the salmon steaks with salt and pepper.
In a separate pan, sear the salmon on both sides over medium-high heat until golden, about 3-4 minutes per side.
The salmon does not need to be cooked through at this point.
Remove the salmon from the pan and let it cool slightly.
Once cool enough to handle, remove the skin and bones, and flake the salmon into bite-sized pieces.
Add the flaked salmon to the pot.
Continue to simmer gently for another 10 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld.
Remove the bay leaves.
Stir in the light cream and heat through, but do not boil.
Taste and adjust seasoning with additional salt and pepper as needed.
Serve the salmon bisque hot, garnished with a sprinkle of fresh herbs if desired.
Enjoy your creamy and flavorful soup!

label: Pasta Peperonata
prep: Begin by roasting the bell peppers.
Preheat your oven to 450°F.
Place the red and yellow bell peppers on a baking sheet and drizzle with olive oil.
Roast in the oven, turning occasionally, until the skins are charred and blistered, about 25-30 minutes.
Remove the peppers from the oven and place them in a bowl.
Cover the bowl with plastic wrap and let the peppers steam for about 10 minutes.
This process will make it easier to peel them.
Once cooled, peel off the skins, remove the seeds, and slice the peppers into thin strips.
While the peppers are roasting, bring a large pot of salted water to a boil.
Cook the rigatoni according to the package instructions until al dente.
Drain and set aside, reserving some pasta water.
In a large skillet, heat a generous drizzle of extra virgin olive oil over medium heat.
Add the thinly sliced red onions and minced garlic cloves.
Sauté until the onions are soft and translucent, about 5-7 minutes.
Add the roasted pepper strips to the skillet.
Stir in the chopped parsley and red wine vinegar, and season with sea salt and black pepper to taste.
Cook for another 5 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld together.
Stir in the grated Parmesan cheese and mascarpone cheese until well combined and the cheeses are melted, creating a creamy sauce.
If the sauce is too thick, add a little reserved pasta water to reach the desired consistency.
Add the cooked rigatoni to the skillet and toss to coat the pasta evenly with the sauce.
Cook together for an additional 2-3 minutes to ensure the pasta is heated through and absorbs some of the flavors.
Serve the Pasta Peperonata hot, garnished with additional Parmesan cheese and a drizzle of extra virgin olive oil if desired.
Enjoy your meal!

label: Greek Fries
prep: Preheat your oven to 425°F.
Wash and cut the potatoes into wedges or thick fries.
Pat dry with paper towels to remove excess moisture.
In a large mixing bowl, toss the potato wedges with 4 tablespoons of olive oil, ensuring all pieces are evenly coated.
Season generously with kosher salt and black pepper.
Spread the potatoes in a single layer on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper.
Bake in the preheated oven for 25-30 minutes, or until golden and crispy, turning halfway through the cooking time.
While the potatoes are baking, heat the remaining 2 tablespoons of olive oil in a small skillet over medium heat.
Add the minced garlic and sauté until fragrant, about 1-2 minutes.
Remove from heat and let it cool.
Once the potatoes are done, transfer them to a large bowl.
Add the sautéed garlic and its oil, chopped parsley, and fresh oregano.
Toss everything together while the fries are still hot, so the herbs and garlic cling to the potatoes.
Transfer the seasoned fries to a serving platter.
Sprinkle crumbled feta cheese over the hot fries.
Serve immediately with a side of tzatziki sauce for dipping.
Enjoy your Greek Fries, a perfect blend of crispy potatoes, aromatic herbs, and the tangy flavors of feta and tzatziki!

label: Parsley Rice
prep: Rinse the basmati rice under cold water until the water runs clear.
This helps remove excess starch and prevents the rice from becoming sticky.
In a medium saucepan, heat the extra virgin olive oil over medium heat.
Add the finely chopped half onion and sauté until the onion is translucent and soft, about 5 minutes.
Stir in the rinsed rice and cook for another 2 minutes, stirring frequently to coat the rice with the oil and to lightly toast it.
Add the sea salt and bay leaf to the saucepan.
Pour in the 1½ cups of chicken or vegetable stock, and bring the mixture to a boil.
Once boiling, reduce the heat to low, cover the saucepan, and let the rice simmer for about 15-18 minutes, or until all the liquid is absorbed and the rice is tender.
Remove the saucepan from the heat.
Discard the bay leaf.
Fluff the rice with a fork to separate the grains.
Stir in the freshly chopped parsley, mixing thoroughly to distribute the herbs evenly throughout the rice.
Let the rice stand covered for 5 minutes before serving to allow the flavors to meld.
Serve the parsley rice warm as a delicious side dish to complement a variety of main courses.
